title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE FIRST CONVOCATION OF AIIMS BILASPUR
subtitle: DEVELOPING AFFORDABLE, ACCESSIBLE, AND COST-EFFECTIVE HEALTHCARE SOLUTIONS PRESENTS AN OPPORTUNITY FOR PREMIER INSTITUTIONS LIKE AIIMS: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 3:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced the first convocation of AIIMS Bilaspur in Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh, today (October 6, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the primary objective of the medical profession should be to serve humanity. She highlighted that a sick person visiting a doctor carries not only the fear and uncertainty associated with their illness but also hope. She emphasised that the empathy and compassionate behaviour of doctors gives courage to the patient, apart from their knowledge and skills that treat the patient. She urged doctors to embrace sensitivity and compassion while striving for excellence in their profession.
The President said that quality medical care at a minimal cost is the hallmark of AIIMS. She said that for the people of the country, AIIMS signifies medical treatment by the nation's most competent doctors. She said that many AIIMS have been established across various parts of the country with the objectives of enabling a larger number of people to benefit from this trust and allowing more meritorious students to receive top-tier medical education and serve the nation.
The President said that AIIMS Bilaspur bears a special responsibility due to its geographical location. Delivering quality healthcare services on time to populations residing in the remote areas of Himachal Pradesh is a multi-faceted challenge. She said that AIIMS Bilaspur must emerge as a premier center for advanced tertiary healthcare. She highlighted the need to strengthen healthcare services in hilly areas by leveraging telemedicine, specialist consultations for remote areas, training of medical personnel, and the use of the latest technologies.
The President said that for the common people, bearing the cost of medical treatment for a serious illness imposes a heavy financial burden. To alleviate this hardship faced by vulnerable sections of society, the Government of India provides health insurance cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year under the ‘Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana’.
The President said that providing quality healthcare to the citizens at an affordable cost is a collective responsibility. The rising cost of medical equipment and medicines poses a serious challenge for patients and their families. Developing affordable, accessible, and cost-effective healthcare solutions presents both a challenge and an opportunity for premier institutions like AIIMS. Through such efforts, our citizens will remain healthy and be able to contribute to the nation's progress to their full potential.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses Second Convocation of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University
subtitle:
“Sanskrit is the Golden String that Connects India’s Many Languages into One Grand Garland”: Vice-President

“Our Ancient Knowledge Must Be Preserved, Studied, Interpreted and Made Available to Future Generations”: Vice-President

“A Favourable Ecosystem Has Been Created for the Resurgence of Sanskrit Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Leadership”: Vice-President

“Use Social Media Wisely; Do Not Let the Virtual World Take You Away from the Real World”: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Second Convocation of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University at Qutub Institutional Area, New Delhi. He congratulated the graduating students, their parents, faculty members and the University community on the occasion. He also led the gathering in taking the “No to Drugs” pledge and presented gold medals to meritorious graduating students.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Second Convocation of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University in New Delhi. 

He highlighted Sanskrit as the “golden string” connecting India’s many languages and emphasised the need to preserve, study and take India’s ancient knowledge traditions to future generations.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 6, 2026
Highlighting the University’s journey from a Sanskrit Vidyapeetha to a Central University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that it was now time for the institution to establish itself as a
leading international centre of excellence for Sanskrit studies
, fulfilling the vision of its founder, former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. Paying tribute to Shri Shastri, he said that his immortal call of “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” was not merely a slogan but reflected India’s resolve to protect its borders and ensure food security.
The Vice-President lauded the University for securing the highest NAAC grade of A++ and for conducting research across diverse domains of the Indian Knowledge Tradition. He said that while every Indian language has enriched the nation, Sanskrit is the “golden string” connecting the pearls of India’s many languages into one grand garland. He also appreciated the University’s efforts to keep Sanskrit alive across the campus through Subhashitas, its 44-year tradition of publishing the Vidyapeeth Panchang, and its teaching of classical disciplines including Prakrit and Vastu Shastra.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised that India’s development must remain rooted in its civilisational heritage. He said that several initiatives under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi have created a favourable ecosystem for the resurgence of Sanskrit and promotion of the Indian Knowledge System. Referring to the National Education Policy 2020 and the Ashtadashi scheme, he said that rare Sanskrit texts must not be allowed to disappear and should be preserved, studied and made accessible to future generations.
Calling for greater scholarly engagement with India’s manuscript heritage, the Vice-President urged the University’s teachers and students to undertake the
discovery, preservation, critical editing and publication of unpublished Sanskrit manuscripts
. Referring to the Gyan Bharatam Mission, he said that the initiative, with a foundational corpus of ₹500 crore for manuscript preservation and documentation, is bringing India’s vast manuscript heritage to the people of India and the world.
Addressing the graduating students, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged them to remain lifelong learners and to carry forward the values imparted by their Acharyas and parents. In the age of Artificial Intelligence, he called upon them to harness technology for the preservation and promotion of Sanskrit.
The Vice-President urged the youth to stay away from drugs and substance abuse, and to choose discipline, sports, good company and meaningful pursuits. He also advised students to use social media wisely and in moderation, investing their time in reading, learning, skill development and building genuine relationships.
During the ceremony, the Vice-President also released three publications:
‘Amnaya Kalpataru’, ‘Vidyamitram’ and ‘Shodha Prabha’ (July–September 2026).
The ceremony was attended by
Shri Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education and DoNER; Prof. Murli Manohar Pathak, Vice-Chancellor of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University; distinguished scholars, Acharyas, officers, faculty members, staff, students, parents and Sanskrit enthusiasts.

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES THE INAUGURAL CEREMONY OF THE SILVER JUBILEE CELEBRATIONS MARKING 25 YEARS OF THE GOA LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY BUILDING
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 8:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Silver Jubilee celebrations programme marking 25 years of the Goa Legislative Assembly Building was inaugurated today by Governor, Goa, Shri Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju.
Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla emphasised that strong democracies are built on dialogue, diverse views and meaningful public participation. Noting that legislatures are forum for discussion, dialogue, debate and exchange of diverse views, he mentioned that democracy becomes stronger when there is space for agreement as well as disagreement, and when diverse perspectives are brought into the legislative process. India's democratic strength, he said, has been built on the ability of its institutions to accommodate diverse opinions and viewpoints.
Referring to India's growing stature in the global arena, Shri Birla said that India's democratic experience and commitment to constitutional values have strengthened the country's voice in the world. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is contributing to finding solutions to global challenges while drawing upon the civilisational ethos of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’. He said that the strength of democracy must ultimately be reflected in the manner in which people's expectations and aspirations are translated into policies, laws and effective governance. He also underlined the special responsibility of elected representatives in smaller States such as Goa, where there is close interaction between representatives and citizens. He urged public representatives to remain sensitive to the aspirations, difficulties and challenges faced by their constituents and work towards their timely resolution.
Stressing that technology can significantly enhance public understanding of legislative processes by enabling citizens to access information relating to rules, laws, policies, legislative debates and the work of committees, Lok Sabha Speaker called for greater transparency and accessibility which can deepen the connection between legislatures and the people. Calling for healthy competition among State Legislatures in adopting innovations, Shri Birla said that legislatures should learn from one another and share best practices in areas such as technology, legislative procedures and institutional reforms. The objective, he said, should be to create a “healthy competition” among legislatures to strengthen democratic institutions.
Lok Sabha Speaker also stressed on greater participation of young people in democratic institutions. He said that India's youth are at the forefront of technology, education, research and innovation, and their participation in the legislative process would contribute to the formulation of better policies and laws. He welcomed the initiative of the Goa Legislative Assembly to organise programmes over four days highlighting the history of the Goa Liberation Movement and the legislative journey of the State. Such initiatives, he said, would help connect young people with legislative institutions and enhance their understanding of the democratic process.
Shri Birla mentioned that Goa has a distinctive identity, known not only for its natural beauty, coastline and rich cultural heritage, but also for its harmonious way of life. He congratulated the present and former Chief Ministers, Speakers, Ministers, Members of Parliament and Members of the Goa Legislative Assembly who have contributed to the State's socio-economic development over the past 25 years. He also acknowledged the contribution of all those elected representatives who, through their debates, views and legislative interventions, have strengthened the dignity and prestige of the Assembly. Shri Birla said that Goa's development journey has been distinctive as the State had to simultaneously promote industry, trade, tourism and education while preserving its rich heritage and natural environment. Maintaining this balance, he said, has been a challenging but important responsibility. He noted that Goa has today established a distinct position in the fields of tourism, industry and education, while also maintaining the dignity and quality of life of its people. He appreciated the efforts of successive governments and elected representatives who have contributed to this journey through policies, legislation and public-oriented initiatives.
Shri Birla noted that the Silver Jubilee should not merely be an occasion to celebrate the Assembly's achievements of the past 25 years, but should also provide an opportunity to envision the next 25 years. He urged the Goa Legislative Assembly to prepare a forward-looking roadmap aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat, with maximum participation of citizens, youth and women. He said that every citizen, particularly the person at the last mile, should feel that the Legislative Assembly is a forum that represents and responds to his or her aspirations and expectations. He  emphasised that the next 25 years should focus on making democratic institutions stronger, more accessible, accountable, responsive and results-oriented. Greater public participation in the functioning of legislatures, he said, would make democratic institutions more accountable and responsible towards citizens.
Congratulating the Goa Legislative Assembly on completing 25 years in its present building, Shri Birla expressed confidence that the Assembly would continue to contribute to Goa's economic and social development while preserving its distinctive culture, heritage and natural environment. He conveyed his greetings to all present and former Members, Speakers, Chief Ministers and other public representatives who have contributed to the development of Goa and strengthened the democratic institutions of the State.
On this occasion, Shri Birla released ‘Customised My Stamp and Special Cover with Special Cancellation’ of the Goa Legislative Assembly and Secretariat Building and also felicitated eminent personalities.
Chief Minister, Goa, Shri Pramod Sawant; Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly, Dr. Ganesh Gaonkar; Minister for Legislative Affairs, Government of Goa, Shri Mauvin Godinho; Leader of Opposition, Goa legislative Assembly, Shri Yuri Alemao and other dignitaries also addressed on the occasion.
Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly, Dr. Ganesh Gaonkar delivered the Welcome Address and Deputy Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly , Shri Joshua Peter De Souza delivered the Words of Gratitude.

title: PM interacts with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board Members
subtitle:
Technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development: PM

Technology-driven solutions needed to tackle cyber fraud: PM

Representatives of Telecom companies Applaud India’s Digital Transformation and Growing Global Technology Partnerships

GSMA Board Members Highlight Opportunities for Global Cooperation with India in 6G and AI
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board members at Seva Teerth earlier today, ahead of the India Mobile Congress. GSMA is a global organisation unifying the mobile ecosystem, representing mobile operators and organisations across the mobile ecosystem and adjacent industries.
Prime Minister emphasised that technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development. He stressed that democratisation of technology is essential to ensure that no section of society is left behind. He underlined the need to make technology and digital services affordable and accessible, particularly for the Global South, and highlighted the importance of taking technology to the last mile to prevent a widening digital divide.
Prime Minister highlighted the potential of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a transformative force, particularly for developing countries. He noted that discussions on DPI with several world leaders had demonstrated its growing global relevance and said that such platforms can serve as a springboard for countries of the Global South.
Addressing the growing challenge of digital and cyber fraud, Prime Minister said the problem requires technology-driven solutions. He suggested sustained awareness messages for users to warn people about potential fraud calls.
Prime Minister also highlighted the need for global standards and common rules for emerging technologies. On the growing threat of deepfakes and AI-generated content, he suggested exploring mechanisms to allow users to immediately identify its origin.
GSMA Board members highlighted India’s emergence as a global leader in digital and mobile connectivity. They noted the rapid expansion of 4G and 5G, the scale of digital public infrastructure and the growth of the telecom and mobile manufacturing ecosystem. They appreciated India’s investment-friendly policy framework and emphasised the role of secure, resilient and trusted digital infrastructure in supporting continued digital growth.
The Board members also highlighted growing opportunities for international cooperation with India in areas including 5G, 6G, AI, cybersecurity, digital inclusion and satellite connectivity.
The meeting was attended by Minister of Communication, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia, Minister of State for Communication, Dr. Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar, GSMA board members  and senior officials of Government of India.

title: Cabinet passes  resolution congratulating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 25 Years of Unbroken Leadership
subtitle: 10 Defining Highlights of the Union Cabinet Resolution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet today passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrates the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by principle of Nation First and Citizen First. Three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive Lok Sabha elections reflect the enduring trust that public have reposed in PM Narendra Modi
These ten salient features capture the unbroken thread connecting his leadership of Gujarat with his leadership of India.
From Gujarat to India A Development Vision Grows
The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarat’s successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens’ grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigram’s separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarat’s experience across India.
Compassion for the Poor Becomes Dignity at Scale
PM Modi’s sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity.
Empowerment Opens Doors Across Society
PM Modi’s determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became LakhpatiDidis, while the Nari Shakti VandanAdhiniyam provided for women’s reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded ₹4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind.
An Unwavering Commitment to Reform
The resolution gives particular emphasis to PM Modi’s willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. His appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. Reform emerges as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose.
Building the Foundations of a Self-Reliant India
Under PM Modi’s leadership, Public capital expenditure rose from ₹2 lakh crore to over ₹12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around ₹2 lakh crore to more than ₹13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen India’s ability to meet its needs.
Technology Serves Citizens and Expands National Ambition
PM Modi’s faith in technology emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. Developing India’s own COVID vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole demonstrated PM Modi’s vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant,
Atmanirbhar Bharat
. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities.
7. Steadfast Leadership Through Turbulent Times
The resolution highlights PM Modi’s ability to give India direction through global upheaval. During COVID, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption. His leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times.
8. Decisive Leadership Secures Peace and Confidence
2016 Surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot Air Strikes and 2025 Operation Sindoor illustrate the national security red lines established under PM Modi. The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, One Rank One Pension and creation of the Chief of Defence Staff’s post. Action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability and public trust.
9. India’s Voice Grows Stronger on the World Stage
The resolution links India’s rising stature with PM Modi’s ability to build cooperation across divisions. Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Union’s G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how India’s capabilities could serve others. Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and India’s growing influence and contribution to shared solutions.
10. Progress Draws Strength from Heritage and Responsibility
PM Modi’s vision unites development, cultural confidence and environmental responsibility. Climate action progressed from Gujarat’s dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships. Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Ram Lalla’s consecration strengthened India’s connection with its heritage. The resolution culminates in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant and developed India by 2047.

title: Cabinet approves Commitment of Rs.10,000 Crore towards establishment of the SME Growth Fund for direct equity investments in Small and Medium Enterprises to create future champions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the Government of India’s commitment of Rs.10,000 crore towards the establishment of the SME Growth Fund (SGF)
aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for India's Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and enabling the emergence of champion Indian enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors, and strategic value chains as per Para 28 of Union Budget 2026-27. This was in part of the holistic set of announcements that were made in Union Budget 2026-27 focussing on providing equity, liquidity and professional support for the MSME ecosystem as a whole.
There are existing funds which provide equity support but majority of them focus on early-stage enterprises and cover majorly Micro enterprises. A structural gap exists for equity growth capital for Small and Medium Enterprises.
The landmark initiative reflects the Government's commitment towards realizing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 by strengthening India's entrepreneurship ecosystem, deepening the domestic capital market for growth-stage enterprises, and creating a new generation of Indian companies capable of competing at the global level.
SMEs constitute the backbone of the Indian economy, contributing significantly to employment generation, exports, manufacturing output, and innovation. While various initiatives have enhanced access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital required by enterprises seeking to scale, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions, and transform into industry leaders. The SME Growth Fund is designed to address this critical financing gap by providing patient growth equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability.
The Fund is envisioned as a transformational instrument to support enterprises at critical inflection points in their growth journey. Majority allocation from SGF will be made towards small and medium manufacturing focused enterprises. Fund will also consider SME’s operating in industrial clusters in Tier II and Tier III cities
By providing long-term capital, the initiative will enable Indian SMEs to scale operations, invest in technology and manufacturing capacity, expand into international markets, integrate into global value chains, and undertake strategic investments. The Government expects the Fund to accelerate the emergence of a strong pipeline of Indian companies with the scale, innovation capability, and competitiveness required to become champions in their respective sectors.
The Government’s commitment to the SME Growth Fund complements its ongoing efforts to strengthen the SME sector through reforms, digitalization initiatives, credit support mechanisms, ease of doing business measures, public procurement reforms, startup promotion initiatives, and production-linked incentive programmes.
Under the initiative, the Government of India will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs.10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework. By enabling manufacturing enterprises to expand capacity, adopt advanced technologies and achieve greater scale, the SGF is expected to improve scale, productivity, and strengthen export competitiveness. Investments across industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, will support balanced regional industrial development, reinforce local supply chains and generate high-quality employment opportunities.
With this initiative, the Government reaffirms its commitment to empowering India's entrepreneurs and fostering a new generation of competitive enterprises. By catalysing investment in high-growth SMEs, the Fund will help create champions, drive innovation-led industrialization, and generate quality employment opportunities across the country. The initiative will serve as a key pillar in advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

title: Cabinet approves setting up of Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 3:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the setting up of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), namely, Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) to strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment within the broad domains of Transportation and Logistics.
The approval seeks to address the long-standing challenges arising from fragmented planning and implementation across multiple transport-related Ministries and agencies.  By fostering greater coordination and multi-modal integration, ITLA is expected to enhance the efficiency, sustainability and effectiveness of transport infrastructure development in India.
ITLA will have following key roles and responsibilities
:
National Apex Institution:
ITLA will function as the apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning, research, project appraisal and monitoring, policy support and data analytics.
Long-Term National Transport Master Plan:
ITLA will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of ten years or more, covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics.
Integrated Planning Framework:
ITLA will evaluate short-term sectoral plans (5 years or so) and annual plans of transport Ministries to ensure consistency and alignment with the National Transport Master Plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.
Technical Appraisal of Major Projects:
ITLA will undertake technical appraisal of infrastructure projects of Government of India, costing Rs.500 crore or more.  Financial appraisal will continue to be carried out through the existing financial appraisal mechanisms.
Monitoring and Impact Assessment:
ITLA will monitor implementation of transport & infrastructure projects above Rs.500 crore and provide a coordinated mechanism for issue resolution and will undertake post-implementation impact assessment of these projects.
National Transport Data Repository (NTDR):
ITLA will build a unified transport data repository by obtaining relevant transport and logistics datasets from multiple sources, including GSTN e-way bill, FASTag, Vahan, GPS-based systems, urban traffic management systems and other relevant databases and carry out data analytics (e.g. Freight Flow/O-D analytics) for planning, monitoring and impact assessment.
Advise and assist for review and updation of National Logistics Policy (2022)
Capacity building, training, and skilling in the logistics sector.
Promote Research & Innovations in transport and logistics sectors.
Establishment of the ITLA will play a pivotal role in realizing India’s Vision 2047 by strengthening multimodal connectivity, improving infrastructure efficiency, reducing logistics costs, and enhancing India’s global logistics competitiveness.  The ITLA will build institutional capacity for research, planning, big data integration, project monitoring, and evaluation, while supporting capacity building and adoption of international best practices.

title: ECI Clarifies Protocol for Meetings with Political Delegations, Says No Political Party Sought Appointment Before 4 PM Today
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 9:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to today's developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission.
Thereafter, at around 4.00 PM, information was received from Delhi Police that a delegation of MPs, led by the Hon'ble Leader of the Opposition, Shri Rahul Gandhi, wished to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum.
In 2025, the Election Commission of India had laid down a procedure for meetings with political parties. All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly Authorised Representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides.
After 4.00 PM today, when the Election Commission was considering the above proposal for the above-mentioned meeting with the Hon'ble MPs, it was informed by the DCP, Delhi Police, that the meeting being sought was to be held with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was the Parliament House Annexe. The Election Commission considered this request as unusual and therefore, could not be accepted, as, in accordance with ECI protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the Election Commission of India.
ECI proposed that its senior-most officer on duty could be sent to the meeting venue to receive the memorandum of the Hon'ble MPs, which in itself would have been an unprecedented step. However, this offer was also declined by the Hon'ble MPs.
ECI respects the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country, as well as its own protocols and conventions, which are of utmost importance. Any political party may, at any time, request for a meeting with the Election Commission; and the Commission, keeping in view the suitability of time, schedules a date and time for the meeting. This is a regular practice.

title: Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s Vision and Sustained Efforts Set the Stage for a New Industrial Era in Gwalior
subtitle:
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah to join Bhoomipujan of Asia’s First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior on 29 October, 2026 at Shri Scindia’s invitation

Shri Scindia’s initiative and sustained efforts are bringing Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone to Gwalior, with 24+ global companies set to participate in the Bhoomipujan together

TMZ has attracted committed investments of over ₹5,500 crore, with the potential to generate 18,000+ employment opportunities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major step towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of an Aatmanirbhar Bharat and strengthening India’s telecom manufacturing capabilities, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s initiative and sustained efforts are giving shape to Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
The Bhoomipujan ceremony for this landmark project will be held on 29 October 2026, in Gwalior with Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah set to participate. Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah has accepted Shri Scindia’s invitation and confirmed his presence at the ceremony.
Conceived as a transformative industrial initiative for Gwalior, the TMZ is the outcome of Shri Scindia’s sustained engagement with the Department of Telecommunications (Ministry of Communications, Government of India), the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the industry. Shri Scindia’s continued efforts of over 2 years have focused on bringing together the required land, infrastructure, investment and industry participation to translate the idea into a world-class telecom manufacturing ecosystem.
Proposed at the Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Counter Magnet City (SADA) in Gwalior, the TMZ is envisioned as a major hub for telecom manufacturing, bringing together manufacturing units, technology innovation, research and development, testing and advanced technology capabilities under one ecosystem.
Union Minister Shri Scindia has been personally driving the project through regular reviews and coordination with senior officials of the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh. From identifying and securing land and developing infrastructure to engaging investors and addressing industry requirements, he has maintained sustained focus on taking the project from concept to now execution with the Bhumipujan ceremony on 29 October 2026.
During his recent inspection of the proposed TMZ site in Gwalior, Union Minister Shri Scindia had underlined that the project was not simply an industrial estate, but a strategic opportunity to create a complete telecom manufacturing ecosystem in Gwalior, bringing together more than 24 manufacturing units and companies associated with the telecom sector.
What is the Telecom Manufacturing Zone?
Similar to how a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) functions, Gwalior's Telecom Manufacturing Zone is being developed on a special plug-and-play model. Under this model, companies will have access to ready infrastructure, common facilities and an enabling industrial environment, allowing them to commence manufacturing operations with minimal lead time.
The TMZ will support manufacturing of telecom equipment and components, while also creating capabilities in design, research and development, testing and innovation. The Zone will also provide a platform for industries associated with optical fibre, semiconductors and advanced technologies such as 5G and 6G.
The initiative is aimed at strengthening India’s domestic telecom manufacturing capacity, advancing self-reliance in telecom products and enhancing India’s participation in global manufacturing and technology value chains.
Union Minister Shri Scindia’s Investor Outreach Brings Investment Proposals of Over ₹5,500 Crore. A key pillar of Union Minister Shri Scindia’s efforts has been his direct engagement with investors and industry leaders to bring investment into the Gwalior TMZ.
Proposed entry (artistic rendition) of the TMZ in Counter Magnet City Area, Gwalior
With the objective of attracting leading companies to the project, Shri Scindia led investor engagements and roadshows in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, presenting the project’s potential, infrastructure and investment opportunities.
In July 2026, the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh signed an MoU for the establishment of the TMZ. This was followed by investor roadshows led by Shri Scindia and Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav.
The Delhi roadshow resulted in investment commitments of approximately ₹3,500 crore, with the potential to generate around 14,000 employment opportunities. At the Mumbai roadshow held on 4 August, companies expressed commitments of approximately ₹2,000 crore, with the potential to create around 4,000 jobs.
More recently, Shri Scindia convened an investor meeting in Bengaluru with companies from the telecom, electronics, semiconductor and technology sectors. The interaction generated further interest in the project, with additional investment proposals of approximately ₹700–800 crore emerging.
As a result of these sustained efforts, the TMZ has now attracted investment proposals exceeding 5,500 crore, with the potential to generate more than 18,000 employment opportunities.
Union Minister Shri Scindia’s investor outreach has helped position the TMZ as a major catalyst for industrial growth and economic activity across the Gwalior-Chambal region.
Central Government to Provide 100% Financial Support of ₹493 Crore
The Government of India is providing 100% financial assistance of ₹493 crore for the infrastructure development of the first phase of the project. The Government of Madhya Pradesh has made approximately 170 acres of land available free of cost for the project.
For implementation, a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) has been constituted with 51% equity participation by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49% by the Department of Telecommunications.
The Centre-State partnership will play a key role in ensuring time-bound implementation, development of industrial infrastructure and provision of essential facilities to investors.
Union Minister Shri Scindia’s Continued Review to Drive Time-Bound Execution
Union Minister Shri Scindia recently conducted a detailed site inspection of the land identified for the TMZ at the Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Counter Magnet City (SADA), along with senior officials from the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh.
During the visit, he reviewed the progress of the project, land availability, requirements of prospective investors and the roadmap ahead. He directed senior officials to ensure that all project-related work moves forward in a time-bound manner and that the infrastructure and facilities required by investors are put in place without delay.
The project continues to remain among Shri Scindia’s key priorities, with regular reviews being undertaken to ensure that the vision for Gwalior’s telecom manufacturing ecosystem translates into a reality on the ground.
A New Chapter in Gwalior’s Industrial Growth
The proposed Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior, driven by Shri Scindia’s vision and sustained efforts, has the potential to transform the region into a significant hub for telecom manufacturing and technology.
Beyond investment, the project is expected to create new opportunities for local youth in employment, technical skills, innovation and entrepreneurship, while strengthening the industrial ecosystem of Gwalior-Chambal and Madhya Pradesh.
Aligned with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and ‘
Make in India, Make for the World
’, the TMZ represents a significant step towards establishing India as a global telecom manufacturing hub.
What began as an ambitious vision championed by Shri Scindia is now taking concrete shape on the ground, with major industry participation, significant investment interest and a clear roadmap for execution. The Gwalior Telecom Manufacturing Zone is poised to become a landmark example of Centre-State cooperation, industry-led growth and India’s transition from telecom consumption to telecom manufacturing and global technology leadership.

date:

                06 OCT 2026 8:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government has appointed Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, PVSM, AVSM, VM, VSM, presently serving as Vice Chief of the Air Staff as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff, in the rank of Air Chief Marshal, with effect from the afternoon of October 31, 2026. The present Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh superannuates from office on October 31, 2026.
Born on December 09, 1966, Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit was commissioned into the fighter stream of Indian Air Force on December 06, 1986. Prior to assuming charge as the Vice Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Dixit served as Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Central Air Command.
The Air Marshal is an alumnus of National Defence Academy, Defence Services Command & Staff College Bangladesh and National Defence College. He has more than 3500 hours of extensive flying experience on various aircraft including, to name a few, Mirage-2000, variants of MiG, Kiran, Jaguar, IL-78, Hawk and Tejas. He is an Experimental Test Pilot and a Qualified Flying Instructor. During his service career spanning approximately four decades, he has been actively involved in numerous operations and exercises including Op-Safed Sagar, Op-Rakshak and Op-Sindoor.
During his illustrious career, the Air Marshal has held a number of significant field and staff appointments. He commanded a frontline fighter air base in Western Sector and a premier fighter training base in Southern Sector. The operational capability of the Indian Air Force has improved with the contribution of the Air Officer in various capacities. He was awarded Vayu Sena Medal in 2006, Vishisht Seva Medal in 2011, Ati Vishisht Seva Medal in 2023 and Param Vishisht Seva Medal in 2026 in recognition of his exemplary and distinguished service.

                06 OCT 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth will inaugurate the 12th National Maritime Search & Rescue Exercise (SAREX-2026) on 07 October 26, and witness SAR Demo off Paradip coast on 08 October 26 being organized by the Indian Coast Guard. A key highlight of this exercise is the international participation of 32 observers from 30 countries, underscoring the cooperative protocols, strategic importance, and global interoperability of the drill.
SAREX-2026 will be one of the largest and most complex SAR exercises ever conducted in the region, deploying 15 Coast Guard ships, two Dornier aircraft, three Advanced Light Helicopters, a Chetak helicopter, IAF C-130J and Mi-17 aircraft, two Indian Navy ships, civil/state assets, and shore-based support units.
The exercise will simulate a Mass Rescue Operation involving concurrent aeronautical and maritime distress situations; including ditching of a passenger aircraft at sea with 228 persons onboard and its impact with container vessel MV Zumba.
The Indian Coast Guard will also convene the 24th National Maritime Search & Rescue (NMSAR) Board Meeting at Bhubaneswar under the Chairmanship of Director General Paramesh Sivamani, Director General, Indian Coast Guard. Deliberations will focus on strengthening national SAR preparedness, enhancing distress-alert management, and ensuring faster mobilisation of rescue assets through technology integration and seamless inter-agency coordination.
The 24th NMSAR Board Meeting and SAREX-2026 highlight India's resolve to build a faster, technology-enabled and internationally connected SAR framework, in consonance with the vision of SAGAR and the spirit of MAHASAGAR.

title: HAL Koraput Delivers 2,000th Aero-Engine, Marking Six Decades of Propulsion Manufacturing
subtitle:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh calls for strengthening indigenous design, development, testing and manufacturing of advanced aero-engines

AL-31FP production capacity to rise from 30 to 50 engines annually with Rs 335 crore investment

Second Shakti engine production line to be established with Rs 218 crore investment; capacity to reach up to 100 engines annually

Government pursuing indigenous high-thrust engine programme with investment of about Rs 5,000 crore
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 4:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh witnessed the delivery of the 2,000th aero-engine by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Koraput Division and announced the establishment of a second production line for Shakti engines on October 06, 2026. Describing the milestone as a significant achievement in India’s aerospace journey, he called for strengthening indigenous capabilities in the design, development, testing, manufacturing and maintenance of advanced aero-engines, stressing that mastery of propulsion technology is essential for self-reliance in the aerospace and defence sector.
Congratulating the engineers, technicians, scientists and skilled workforce of HAL Koraput, Shri Rajnath Singh said the delivery of 2,000 engines represents 2,000 significant contributions to the operational capability of the Defence Forces and reflects six decades of engineering expertise and technological experience since the Division was established in 1964.
The Raksha Mantri highlighted HAL Koraput’s contribution to military aviation, noting that its engines have powered frontline aircraft including the MiG-21, MiG-27, MiG-29 and Su-30MKI. He stated that while production provides new capability, overhaul extends service life, making both critical for military preparedness. He appreciated HAL Koraput’s indigenous repair and overhaul capability, with more than 9,000 engines overhauled so far, and noted that indigenisation of components and reduced turnaround time are contributing to operational readiness and extended service life of critical defence assets.
Describing the aero-engine as the ‘heart’ of an aircraft, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that reliable propulsion is essential to effectively utilise advanced airframes, radars, weapons and avionics. He highlighted the need for expertise in precision manufacturing, advanced materials, metallurgy, cooling technologies, testing and stringent quality assurance. He noted that aero-engine technology combines advanced superalloys, thermal-barrier coatings and sophisticated cooling systems for reliable performance under extreme conditions, making mastery of propulsion technology a mastery of some of the most advanced industrial capabilities.
Raksha Mantri underlined that aerospace self-reliance must extend to indigenous aero-engine capability, particularly for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme. He highlighted the proposed investment of around Rs 5,000 crore, indigenisation of raw materials in partnership with Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited (MIDHANI) and establishment of India’s first indigenous high-thrust engine testing facility. He stressed that a sovereign aerospace ecosystem requires indigenous capabilities across materials, design, manufacturing, testing and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO).
Highlighting HAL’s performance in meeting Defence Forces’ requirements, Shri Rajnath Singh noted that the Government placed an order for 240 AL-31FP engines with HAL in 2024 for the Su-30MKI. Despite global supply-chain disruptions and raw-material challenges, HAL delivered the first engine ahead of schedule and has delivered 63 engines against a target of 60 by the end of the second year.
Raksha Mantri announced that HAL is enhancing annual AL-31FP production capacity from 30 to 50 engines with an investment of Rs 335 crore. He also announced a second Shakti engine production line with an investment of Rs 218 crore. The new line will manufacture up to 100 engines annually and is scheduled to be fully established by 2028-29, catering to indigenous helicopters including Dhruv Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) and Prachand Light Combat Helicopter (LCH).
Emphasising the need for reliable indigenous propulsion for India’s helicopter ecosystem, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the Defence Forces require engines that are available when needed, supported throughout their lifecycle and upgraded with evolving technology. He noted that aero-engine development is a long-term endeavour requiring sustained investment, specialised testing, skilled manpower and a strong industrial ecosystem, with focus on repeatable, reliable and scalable production, design, critical materials and superalloys.
Raksha Mantri called for greater integration of MSMEs, start-ups, private industry, academia and research institutions into the propulsion ecosystem. He called upon HAL to develop Koraput not merely as an engine production facility but as a broader aerospace propulsion ecosystem by nurturing suppliers, mentoring MSMEs, supporting start-ups and young engineers, collaborating with universities and research institutions, and developing capabilities for critical components.
Highlighting Odisha’s growing importance in the defence and aerospace ecosystem, Shri Rajnath Singh noted the State’s strategic location, long coastline, ports, mineral resources, industrial infrastructure and skilled manpower. He stated that strategic infrastructure, including DRDO’s Integrated Test Range at Chandipur, along with recent initiatives of the Odisha Government, provides a strong foundation for growth of the aerospace and defence manufacturing ecosystem.
Appreciating the initiatives of the Odisha Government, under Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Raksha Mantri highlighted the approval for an Aerospace and Defence Equipment Manufacturing Complex at Gajamara, Dhenkanal. He called upon HAL to develop Koraput as a nucleus of a broader aerospace propulsion ecosystem by developing suppliers, mentoring MSMEs, providing opportunities to young engineers and start-ups in advanced technology areas, collaborating with universities and research institutions, creating opportunities for skilled local youth, and developing indigenous manufacturing capabilities for critical engine components.
Urging the HAL Koraput team to raise standards in quality, productivity, indigenisation, innovation and delivery timelines, Shri Rajnath Singh described the 2,000th engine as a significant milestone and called for using it as a foundation to build an Indian aerospace industry capable of designing, developing, manufacturing and supporting advanced propulsion systems. He congratulated the HAL Koraput team, Indian Air Force, industry partners, MSMEs, scientists, engineers, technicians and the people of Odisha on the occasion.
Chief Minister of Odisha Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Deputy Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Tejpal Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD), HAL Shri Ravi K, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD), MIDHANI Dr. S.V.S. Narayana Murty and Joint Secretary (Aerospace Wing & DOMW) Ms Manisha Chandra were also present on the occasion.

title: DRDO Conducts Maiden Live Jump of Advanced High-Altitude Parachute
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the maiden live jump of the Advanced High-Altitude Parachute (AHAP) at one of the highest-altitude drop zones, Nyoma (Mudh DZ).
The jump was executed at 16,000 feet above mean sea level (AMSL). The parachute was deployed at 15500 feet AMSL and landing was undertaken at Nyoma (Mudh DZ) which is at 13,700 feet. The jump proved the efficacy and tactical employability of the AHAP parachute at extremely High-Altitude Terrains.
Designed and developed by Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE), Agra, AHAP is a static line parachute system for mass drop of paratroopers.
The system has been manufactured by Ordnance Parachute Factory (OPF) Kanpur, inspected by DGAQA and certified by CEMILAC, RCMA Kanpur.
AHAP offers various deployment modes, has a very wide operational altitude range (up to 18000 ft) and has the safest rate of descent especially suited for the tactical requirements of the Indian Defence Forces for high-altitude terrains. Static line parachute jumps at these high altitudes are complex and inherently risky owing to very high opening shock and rate of descent.
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh complimented DRDO, Defence Forces, DPSUs and Industry on the successful maiden live jump of AHAP indigenous parachute system and termed it as another big step towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D & Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh congratulated the team members associated with the design and development of the system.

title: DRDO Conducts Flight Trial of High-Altitude Platform
date:

                06 OCT 2026 3:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has carried out the successful flight trial of indigenously developed High-Altitude Platform (HAPS). The experimental flight attained an altitude of 21 km above mean sea level (AMSL) and remained at an altitude of 20 km AMSL for more than 30 minutes, before it was commanded to descend back to ground. The system was successfully recovered and flight performance data was analyzed.
Real-time video data and all other vehicle parameters were acquired from the Airborne platform at Ground Control Station during the entire flight, which showed intended flight performance. The trial was conducted in coordination with various agencies, namely Indian Air Force, CEMILAC, DGCA, Airports Authority of India (AAI) and other civil authorities.
The High-Altitude Platform, a lighter than air system as a long endurance stratospheric aerial surveillance platform, is being designed and developed by Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE), Agra.

title: Raksha Mantri launches first indigenous Fleet Support Ship ‘ Surya’ at Hindustan Shipyard Ltd in Visakhapatnam
subtitle:
“The launch of FSS1 is a symbol of achievement, keel laying of FSS5 is a symbol of resolve and the new Slipway is a symbol of our growing capability”: Shri Rajnath SIngh

“We must make HSL a benchmark for Quality, Productivity and Timely Delivery”

“Visakhapatnam should be developed as a major Maritime Industrial Hub”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 12:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh launched the first Fleet Support Ship (FSS-1), laid the keel of the fifth Fleet Support Ship (FSS-5) and inaugurated the upgraded Slipway-4 and 300-tonne Goliath Crane at Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), Visakhapatnam on October 06, 2026. The milestone is a significant step in strengthening HSL’s capacity to build larger and more complex ships and advancing India’s indigenous maritime capability.
Addressing the gathering, the Raksha Mantri said the three milestones had significance beyond the individual achievements.
“The launch of FSS1 is a symbol of achievement, keel laying of FSS5 is a symbol of resolve and the new Slipway is a symbol of our growing capability,”
he said, adding that HSL was strengthening not only its shipbuilding capacity but also the foundation of India’s maritime power.
Recalling the launch of  the first ship built in independent India ‘Jala Usha’ at Visakhapatnam in 1948, RM highlighted India’s longstanding maritime heritage, noting that the country’s relationship with the sea dates back to ancient times. He described HSL as a custodian of India’s national maritime capability and lauded its contribution to the country’s maritime and defence requirements for more than eight decades. RM highlighted HSL’s attainment of Miniratna Category-I status in 2025 after it came under the Ministry of Defence as an important milestone reflecting its transformation and sustained efforts.
Fleet Support Ships to strengthen Navy’s reach and endurance
Highlighting the Fleet Support Ship programme, the Raksha Mantri said the vessels would strengthen the Navy’s reach, endurance and operational effectiveness in the Indian Ocean Region. He noted that a Navy operating for extended periods in distant maritime areas requires not only warships but also logistics, maintenance, sustained support and operational endurance. Fleet Support Ships provide this essential capability through at-sea replenishment and sustained support to naval operations. RM underscored the launch of FSS-1 as an important step towards strengthening the Navy’s operational reach and endurance, while the keel laying of FSS-5 representing another strong foundation for India’s maritime future.
FSS-1, named ‘Surya’, was launched following the traditional honours performed by Smt. Laila Swaminathan, President, Navy Wives Wellness Association (NWWA). The vessel entered the waters of the Bay of Bengal amid cheers from the gathering. Designed and built indigenously by HSL, the Fleet Support Ships will feature enhanced cargo and fluid capacity, onboard first-line maintenance workshops, a helicopter deck for Multi-Role Helicopter operations and self-defence systems.
Enhanced infrastructure to support larger shipbuilding programmes
The upgraded Slipway-4 has been extended and strengthened to enable HSL to build and launch ships of up to 45,000 DWT.  The 300-tonne Goliath Crane spanning Slipways 3 and 4 has been designed and manufactured by M/s L&T Geostructure with Konecranes under Make in India. Equipped with PLC controls, Variable Frequency Drives, tandem lifting, remote diagnostics and condition monitoring, the crane will enable faster and more precise handling of heavier blocks for modern block construction. The new infrastructure will strengthen HSL’s ability to undertake larger and more complex shipbuilding programmes and support modern block construction.
Andhra Pradesh to play a larger role in India’s maritime future
“Self-reliance is an important milestone, but global competitiveness is the next big leap,” said RM while stressing that Indian shipyards should be able to compete on quality, cost, technology, delivery and reliability with the world’s leading shipyards.
The Raksha Mantri called for HSL to become more closely integrated with Andhra Pradesh’s wider industrial ecosystem. He said the State’s MSMEs could become suppliers, universities could contribute to research and skill development, technology companies could support digital shipbuilding and startups could develop maritime technologies. He said the objective should be to develop a complete shipbuilding ecosystem around HSL, supported by logistics, port infrastructure, research, technology and skilled manpower.
Emphasising Visakhapatnam’s strategic importance, the Raksha Mantri said the presence of the Eastern Naval Command, Naval Dockyard, HSL and Visakhapatnam Port provides the city with the foundation of a Integrated maritime ecosystem. He called for Visakhapatnam to be developed as a major Maritime Industrial Hub by bringing together naval expertise, shipbuilding capability, engineering talent, port infrastructure and skilled manpower. RM also stressed the need for an integrated national maritime ecosystem involving the Navy, HSL, DRDO, academia, industry, MSMEs and startups. “India’s maritime strength cannot be built by the Navy or shipyards alone,” he said, calling for greater integration among all stakeholders.
“Our goal should be simple and clear- Design better. Build faster. Deliver on time. Operate efficiently and do Maintenance effectively,” said RM. He highlighted that India’s defence manufacturing
ecosystem had undergone significant transformation over the past decade, with increasing focus on domestic design and manufacture of sophisticated systems and platforms. He identified timely delivery, productivity, indigenous design capability, supply chain resilience, skilled manpower, capacity and cost competitiveness as key areas that would determine India’s ability to convert its shipbuilding potential into global competitiveness.
Outlining priorities for HSL, he called for timely delivery to become an organisational culture, greater learning from leading global shipyards, stronger indigenous design capability, partnerships with MSMEs and startups, and development of lifecycle capability. He also emphasised the importance of closer coordination between the Navy and shipyards.
The Raksha Mantri further said India’s objective should go beyond self-reliance to global competitiveness. Approved by the Government of India in March 2024, the IndiaAI Mission is driving the country's vision of becoming a global leader in artificial intelligence by fostering innovation, enabling responsible AI development, strengthening indigenous AI capabilities, and ensuring that the benefits of AI reach every section of society.
A key pillar of the Mission, AIKosh serves as India's unified data platform, providing access to high-quality datasets, AI models, toolkits, benchmarks and other critical resources that support research and AI application development. Through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, the IndiaAI Mission seeks to introduce students and academic institutions to these national AI assets while encouraging hands-on learning and innovation.
As part of the programme, 160+ students from NIT Andhra Pradesh participated in expert sessions, live demonstrations and hands-on activities designed to familiarise them with AIKosh and the broader IndiaAI ecosystem. Participants also explored the AIKosh MCP (Model Context Protocol) and AIKosh SDK (Software Development Kit), which enable users to discover datasets and AI models using natural language, simplifying access to national AI resources and lowering barriers for both developers and non-developers.
Speaking on the initiative, Shri Md. Y. Safirulla K IAS, Director, IndiaAI Mission, said: "Guided by the vision of our Honourable Prime Minister to democratize AI, the IndiaAI Mission continues to carry this commitment to campuses across the country. They will also be encouraged to enrich existing datasets and develop proof-of-concept AI applications addressing public-good use cases. Outstanding student-led contributions may be considered for future recognition, creating a pathway from AI literacy and dataset exploration to innovation and real-world problem solving.

Today, AIKosh hosts 16,000+ Datasets, 350+ AI models and 200+ use cases, enabling researchers, startups, developers and students to build AI solutions using trusted national resources.
The programme at NIT Andhra Pradesh marks another step towards building a vibrant AI-ready talent pool and advancing the IndiaAI Mission's vision of creating an inclusive, responsible and innovation-driven AI ecosystem for the nation. Through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, the Mission will continue to engage academic institutions across the country, fostering campus-level AI communities that contribute to datasets, models, applications, research and responsible AI adoption.

content:
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has issued an
o
rder mandating expansion of Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras at industries in the National Capital Region (NCR) to ensure comprehensive real-time monitoring of fuel consumption and compliance with
its d
irections. The measure is aimed at strengthening vigilance, monitoring and compliance by industries, particularly in view of the adverse impact of industrial emissions on air quality in the NCR and
adjoining areas,
which assumes greater significance during the winter months.
In view of the persistent use of unapproved fuels, the Commission has expanded the areas to be captured by PTZ cameras at industrial units to make the coverage comprehensive and for effective monitoring and compliance. Apart from the locations of PTZ cameras already prescribed by CPCB, the Commission has directed that industries shall now also install additional PTZ cameras
by 31.10.2026
, as per the following Standard Operating Procedure (SOP):
Location of Cameras
Cameras will be installed to capture all fuel storage areas.
Cameras will be installed to capture all fuel charging points.
In case of use of gas-based fuel, the gauge/ meter of the gas is to be captured by the camera.
Real Time Streaming
Real-time streaming of video feeds shall be made available to the servers of CPCB and respective SPCBs/ DPCC.
Power Source
All industries shall ensure that these cameras and the connectivity have adequate power backup.
The Order also mandates CPCB and the concerned SPCBs/ DPCC to develop portals and other necessary infrastructure to capture the real-time streaming of video feeds. This will facilitate remote monitoring of fuel-use practices by industries and help in ensuring the compliance of Commission’s Statutory Directions. The status of implementation of the said measures shall be submitted to the Commission by the concerned SPCBs/ DPCC by
01.11.2026
.
In the light of pollution caused by industrial emissions, the Commission had also prescribed a standard list of approved fuels for NCR for various applications, including industrial use. However, the Flying Squads of the Commission, during incognito inspections of industries across the NCR, have reported use of unapproved fuels in multiple instances. In view of the persistent use of unapproved fuels, the Commission has considered real-time monitoring of fuel consumption by industries necessary.
Considering the poor air quality in Delhi-NCR and with a view to ensure strict vigilance, monitoring and compliance through self-regulation, the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) had earlier directed installation of Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras along with real-time Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) by industries. The prescribed locations for installation of PTZ cameras include capturing the OCEMS port-hole as well as flue gas emissions from the stack in case of textile and food processing units having boilers and capturing fume extraction system areas and furnace feeding areas in metal units.

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav is leading the Indian Delegation at the UNFCCC’s Pre-COP31 meetings being co-hosted by Australia, Fiji and Tuvalu.
Addressing the Leaders’ Plenary at Fiji, the Union Minister today called for equal attention to adaptation, mitigation and means of implementation as the world moves towards COP31. He emphasized that the principles of Equity and Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) must be upheld in letter and spirit for meaningful and sustained climate action across countries.
Shri Yadav stressed that there cannot be a “one-size-fits-all” pathway to climate action. He highlighted that local studies and assessments are important for finding solutions to emerging challenges of the area. These solutions, in turn,  indicate the mitigation and adaptation measures required and the commensurate resources required for the same, he added.
The Union Minister said India, with its vast coastline and islands, fully understands the challenges faced by Pacific Island Countries. He informed that India has developed a broad knowledge base and expertise in the area of ocean science through our premier institutions and bodies like Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM), National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR).
Shri Yadav highlighted that India has developed knowledge and expertise in vulnerability assessment of coasts, mapping of shoreline changes, development of marine spatial plans, integrated management plans for coastal areas and unlocking the potential of the Blue Economy. Further, he stated, India is also using its space ecosystem, Earth-observation capabilities and space-based applications for shoreline monitoring, inundation assessment, cyclone and extreme-weather early warning, and climate-risk assessment. He offered to share this knowledge and expertise with its Pacific partners.
The Minister said India has always stood firmly with its Pacific partners and is working closely with them in areas including health and wellness, renewable energy, resilient infrastructure, early warning, IT, agriculture and capacity building. Referring to his visit to Tuvalu, Shri Yadav said the Tuvalu Coastal Adaptation Project was a strong reflection of how international cooperation, particularly the provision of means of implementation, can translate into tangible resilience on the ground. The Minister reiterated that the experience has reinforced the importance of finding local solutions to emerging climate challenges.
Pre-COP is a preparatory meeting held a few weeks before the annual UN Climate Change Conference, which this year will be held in Antalya, Türkiye, in November.

date:

                06 OCT 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the Government of India’s commitment of Rs.10,000 crore towards the establishment of the SME Growth Fund (SGF)
aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for India's Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and enabling the emergence of champion Indian enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors, and strategic value chains as per Para 28 of Union Budget 2026-27. This was in part of the holistic set of announcements that were made in Union Budget 2026-27 focussing on providing equity, liquidity and professional support for the MSME ecosystem as a whole.
There are existing funds which provide equity support but majority of them focus on early-stage enterprises and cover majorly Micro enterprises. A structural gap exists for equity growth capital for Small and Medium Enterprises.
The landmark initiative reflects the Government's commitment towards realizing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 by strengthening India's entrepreneurship ecosystem, deepening the domestic capital market for growth-stage enterprises, and creating a new generation of Indian companies capable of competing at the global level.
SMEs constitute the backbone of the Indian economy, contributing significantly to employment generation, exports, manufacturing output, and innovation. While various initiatives have enhanced access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital required by enterprises seeking to scale, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions, and transform into industry leaders. The SME Growth Fund is designed to address this critical financing gap by providing patient growth equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability.
The Fund is envisioned as a transformational instrument to support enterprises at critical inflection points in their growth journey. Majority allocation from SGF will be made towards small and medium manufacturing focused enterprises. Fund will also consider SME’s operating in industrial clusters in Tier II and Tier III cities
By providing long-term capital, the initiative will enable Indian SMEs to scale operations, invest in technology and manufacturing capacity, expand into international markets, integrate into global value chains, and undertake strategic investments. The Government expects the Fund to accelerate the emergence of a strong pipeline of Indian companies with the scale, innovation capability, and competitiveness required to become champions in their respective sectors.
The Government’s commitment to the SME Growth Fund complements its ongoing efforts to strengthen the SME sector through reforms, digitalization initiatives, credit support mechanisms, ease of doing business measures, public procurement reforms, startup promotion initiatives, and production-linked incentive programmes.
Under the initiative, the Government of India will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs.10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework. By enabling manufacturing enterprises to expand capacity, adopt advanced technologies and achieve greater scale, the SGF is expected to improve scale, productivity, and strengthen export competitiveness. Investments across industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, will support balanced regional industrial development, reinforce local supply chains and generate high-quality employment opportunities.
With this initiative, the Government reaffirms its commitment to empowering India's entrepreneurs and fostering a new generation of competitive enterprises. By catalysing investment in high-growth SMEs, the Fund will help create champions, drive innovation-led industrialization, and generate quality employment opportunities across the country. The initiative will serve as a key pillar in advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.
