content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, today conferred degrees on the first graduating batch of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Bilaspur at the Institute’s first Convocation, marking a major milestone in the growth of the institution and its contribution to medical education and healthcare in the country.
Addressing the graduating students, the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, lauded the graduates and the gold medallists, as well as the parents, guardians and teachers who supported them through their academic course. She stated that, as the first batch to graduate from AIIMS Bilaspur, they have a special role in shaping the identity and legacy of the institution. She implored them to uphold its reputation through their conduct, commitment and service, reminding them that the medical profession carries a responsibility towards humanity.
She encouraged the graduates to keep the needs of people at the centre of their work, particularly those living in remote and inaccessible areas with limited access to specialised healthcare. Given the geographical location of AIIMS Bilaspur, she asked the Institute and its graduates to work towards strengthening tertiary healthcare in the region, including through telemedicine, expert consultations, training of medical personnel and the use of modern technology.
The President also highlighted the role of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana in reducing the financial burden of healthcare for economically vulnerable families, under which eligible beneficiaries receive health cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year. She noted that more than ₹2 lakh crore has been spent on treatment under the scheme and asked stakeholders to endorse that information about these health protection measures reaches people in far flung areas. She also stressed the need for leading institutions such as AIIMS to contribute to the development of basic and cost effective healthcare solutions.
Exhorting the graduates to remain lifelong learners, the President asked them to keep pace with changing medical practices and health services, while translating research into innovation that improves people's lives. "The field of medicine is not just a field of science and technology. It is actually a field of compassion and trust as well," she said.
Governor of Himachal Pradesh Shri Kavinder Gupta commended the graduates on their achievement and highlighted the important role being played by AIIMS Bilaspur in bringing specialised healthcare closer to people in Himachal Pradesh and neighbouring states, particularly those from remote and tribal areas. Recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s remarks on the occasion of AIIMS Bilaspur’s inauguration, he noted that the Institute is extensively contributing to healthcare, education and research and has strengthened Himachal’s footing in the health sector.
Conveying his regards to the graduating students, he reminded them that their degrees carry a responsibility towards society and the nation and urged them to place compassion, sensitivity and service at the centre of their professional journeys. He expressed confidence that the graduates would use their knowledge and service spirit to contribute to the nation and said, “I believe that these graduate students of AIIMS Bilaspur will make a new identity with their talent, their knowledge and their service spirit in various fields of the country and will make an important contribution in the construction of a Viksit Bharat.”
Speaking at the Occasion, Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda expressed happiness and pride at witnessing the inaugural batch of AIIMS Bilaspur complete its academic journey. Highlighting the expansion of medical education in the country, he shared that the number of medical colleges has increased from 384 to over 800, while undergraduate medical seats have risen from 51,348 to 1.42 lakh. Addressing the gathering, he shared the Government’s target of adding 75,000 undergraduate and postgraduate medical seats by 2029, including an allocation of ₹15,000 crore for the creation of 10,000 additional MBBS and PG seats.
Highlighting the expansion of the AIIMS network under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Minister noted that while the country had only one AIIMS for several decades, 16 new AIIMS have been established in the last 12 years. He urged the audience to recognise the scale of this expansion and the efforts to widen access to quality medical education and specialised healthcare across the country.
Speaking about AIIMS Bilaspur, Shri Nadda noted that the Institute has expanded beyond its initial target of 750 beds and now has 776 beds, with 26 specialties and 15 super specialties fully functional. He highlighted the availability of complex surgical procedures, cardiac catheterisation interventions, neurosurgery, comprehensive care, cancer care and radiotherapy services, noting that this progress has been achieved within the last five years. He also shared that the Institute’s OPD consultations have crossed 12 lakh and IPD admissions have crossed 1 lakh over the last four years.
Shri Nadda spoke highly of the AIIMS Bilaspur faculty and staff for the pace at which the Institute has developed and expressed confidence in its continued growth. Addressing the graduating students, he urged them to uphold the reputation of AIIMS Bilaspur and carry its values of excellence and service into their professional journeys. “With your rapid growth, I am certain that very soon AIIMS Bilaspur will be at par with any other AIIMS in the country” he said, while expressing confidence that the graduates would provide high quality services and work for humanity.
Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh Shri Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu also extended his best wishes to the graduating students and AIIMS Bilaspur on the occasion.
Gracing the event, Shri Harsh Mahajan, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, Lt Gen (Dr.) Daljit Singh (Retd.), Executive Director, AIIMS Bilaspur and Prof. (Dr.) Narendra Kumar Arora, President, AIIMS Bilaspur, were also present.
A total of 92 students received their degrees at the ceremony: 43 MBBS, 26 BSc Honours Nursing, 9 BSc Allied Healthcare and 14 MD/MS students. The President also presented Gold Medals to meritorious students across disciplines in recognition of their academic performance. The awardees included Ms. Sagarika and Mr. Rakshit Vashishth from MBBS, Ms. Bhawna Thakral from BSc Allied Healthcare Science, Ms. Bhavya Malhotra from BSc Honours Nursing and Mr. Prateek Goel from MD, Community & Family Medicine.
About AIIMS Bilaspur
AIIMS Bilaspur began its academic endeavour with the induction of its first MBBS batch in January 2021, followed by the first batches of Allied Healthcare Sciences and Nursing Sciences in 2022. The Institute was formally inaugurated in October 2022 in the presence of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Since then, it has steadily expanded its academic, clinical and research capacities.
During 2024 to 2025, the Institute recorded more than 3 lakh OPD consultations and provided emergency medical services to over 17,000 people. More than 3,500 major surgeries, over 900 minor surgeries, more than 1,000 cardiac catheterisation procedures and over 3,200 dialysis sessions were carried out during the year, while its diagnostic laboratories conducted more than 10 lakh tests. The Institute currently has around 620 students pursuing various undergraduate, postgraduate and super specialty courses, reflecting its growing role in medical education alongside healthcare delivery.
The Convocation marks a significant step in AIIMS Bilaspur’s institutional journey, as its pioneering batch moves from academic training into professional service. The newly qualified doctors, nurses, allied healthcare professionals and postgraduate specialists will attend patients and strengthen public health across the country.

. The achievement reflects the growing role of telemedicine in complementing the country’s existing healthcare delivery system and in overcoming barriers of distance, geography and access, particularly for citizens living in rural, remote and underserved areas.
As the world’s largest telemedicine implementation in primary healthcare, eSanjeevani has emerged as an important component of India’s digital health ecosystem. By enabling citizens to consult healthcare professionals remotely, the platform has extended the reach of public healthcare services beyond the physical boundaries of conventional health facilities and brought medical consultations closer to people in the communities where they live.
The service has witnessed rapid and sustained expansion since its inception. eSanjeevani currently supports more than 1.42 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir spokes, 19,473 medical hubs and 901 online OPDs, with 2,41,923 registered healthcare providers. Available in 15 languages, including English and 14 Indian languages, the platform is facilitating approximately 2.5–3 lakh consultations every day. Its highest single-day utilisation has reached 6,30,315 consultations, reflecting the increasing acceptance and utilisation of telemedicine services across the country.
The utilisation pattern of eSanjeevani also highlights its growing relevance among population groups for whom access to physical healthcare facilities may involve greater travel, time or logistical challenges. Women account for 57.14 per cent of total utilisation, while 40.15 per cent of consultations are availed by citizens aged 46 years and above, including 16.25 per cent by senior citizens aged 60 years and above. The significant participation of women and older citizens underscores the potential of telemedicine to make healthcare more convenient and accessible while complementing services available through the public health system.
The platform has continued to evolve with the integration of emerging technologies aimed at strengthening the quality of telemedicine services. A key recent advancement is the integration of an Artificial Intelligence-powered Clinical Decision Support System (AI-CDSS), which supports healthcare providers during consultations and assists in strengthening the quality, consistency and efficiency of clinical decision-making. The innovation has received national recognition with the Gold Award under the National Awards for e-Governance 2026.
In another significant step towards strengthening integrated healthcare delivery, eSanjeevani has also been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS)-112, enabling stronger linkages between emergency response services and remote medical expertise. The integration is aimed at facilitating more coordinated access to medical support and further strengthening the use of digital technology in emergency healthcare.
Building on its extensive primary healthcare network, eSanjeevani is now expanding beyond primary healthcare to facilitate specialist OPD consultations through premier government medical institutions. Patient-to-doctor teleconsultation services for select specialities have been rolled out at AIIMS Jodhpur, AIIMS Jammu and AIIMS Patna, enabling patients to access specialist consultations remotely from their homes.
The initiative is expected to reduce the need for patients to undertake long-distance travel and wait for consultations at tertiary-care facilities, while improving access to specialist medical expertise. The facility is envisaged for progressive expansion to other premier government institutions, including AIIMS, JIPMER and PGIMER Chandigarh, thereby complementing conventional in-person OPD services and strengthening the continuum of care.
The expansion of specialist teleconsultation services marks an important evolution in the journey of eSanjeevani. From facilitating consultations at the primary healthcare level, the platform is increasingly enabling linkages across different levels of care, helping connect patients with appropriate medical expertise while making more effective use of the specialist capacity available within the public healthcare system.
eSanjeevani is a Made-in-India digital health solution developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), with C-DAC Mohali providing end-to-end technological development and engineering support since its inception. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has played a central role in guiding the continuous evolution of the platform in response to the emerging needs of India’s healthcare system.
Through sustained collaboration between the Ministry and technology partners, coupled with continuous innovation, eSanjeevani has evolved from its initial hub-and-spoke telemedicine model into a population-scale national digital health platform serving 50 crore consultations. The development and scaling of the platform reflects India’s growing capability to design and deploy indigenous digital public infrastructure for large-scale public healthcare delivery and is aligned with the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the vision of a Viksit Bharat.
The achievement of 50 crore teleconsultations marks a significant milestone in India’s digital health journey and reflects the growing role of technology in strengthening the country’s public healthcare system. With its expanding reach across primary and specialist care, integration of Artificial Intelligence and emergency response services, and continued expansion to premier tertiary-care institutions, eSanjeevani is emerging as an important enabler of accessible and equitable healthcare.
The continued evolution of the platform underscores the Government’s commitment to harnessing digital public infrastructure and indigenous technological capabilities to bridge geographical barriers, strengthen the continuum of care and advance the goal of Universal Health Coverage, ensuring that quality healthcare is brought closer to citizens across the country.

title: Chintan Shivir 2026 Concludes with Focus on Collaborative Knowledge Sharing for Quality Road Infrastructure
subtitle: Two-day conclave provides platform for Centre, States and stakeholders to share experiences, best practices and practical solutions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The two-day “Chintan Shivir 2026 – A National Conclave on Highway Infrastructure” concluded today at Statue of Unity, Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, with a renewed focus on strengthening Centre-State collaboration, sharing field-level experiences and building institutional capacity for delivery of quality road infrastructure.
In his valedictory address, Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Shri V. Umashankar, said the Chintan Shivir has provided an opportunity to create a common community of the highways and road sector, enabling States and other stakeholders to share initiatives, experiences and solutions at the policy as well as implementation levels.
Shri Umashankar highlighted that the focus of infrastructure development is increasingly shifting towards quality, with the vision of Viksit Bharat requiring high-quality roads across urban and rural areas, State Highways, National Highways and Expressways.
A key outcome of the deliberations was the opportunity for States to leverage technology platforms and institutional capabilities developed at the national level. Platforms such as PM GatiShakti, Data Lake, eDAR, contractor rating systems and Bhoomi Rashi can be made available for State-level applications, with technical handholding and capacity-building support.
The AI-enabled eDAR platform, currently being used for the National Highway network, can also support States in analysing accident patterns on State and local roads and developing evidence-based interventions for improving road safety, subject to availability of relevant road data.
The deliberations also highlighted the need to strengthen the construction ecosystem through professionalisation, skill development and improved supervision. Shri Umashankar emphasised the importance of focused skill development and capacity building among construction workers to enhance construction practices and ensure better quality outcomes.
Emphasis was also placed on strengthening the quality-based selection and performance assessment of DPR consultants, Authority Engineers and Independent Engineers, with greater weightage to technical capability and past performance. These measures are aimed at addressing gaps in supervision and ensuring better project outcomes.
The conclave further discussed the scope for States to adopt innovative contracting and financing mechanisms, including Model Concession Agreements, BOT and Annuity-based models, particularly for the development of State Highways and State Expressways. The experience and expertise developed at the national level can be utilised by States through structured handholding and capacity-building.
Shri Umashankar also invited States to organise their own Chintan Shivirs and workshops, with participation from domain experts and officers to facilitate knowledge exchange and wider adoption of successful practices.
The two-day conclave featured thematic sessions on PM GatiShakti and integrated infrastructure planning; Land Acquisition and Bhoomi Rashi; Model Concession Agreements and Ratings; Designing Safe Highways, Green Highways, Road Safety and Toll Reform; and Quality Assurance and Project Monitoring.
The sessions facilitated Centre-State dialogue, exchange of best practices and identification of practical and replicable solutions to implementation challenges, reinforcing a collaborative approach towards building future-ready, safe and high-quality road infrastructure in the country.

title: Ministry of Rural Development Notifies 375 Permissible Works under VB–G RAM G
subtitle:
The new Schedule expands the scope of permissible works by 41 percent compared with the previous scheme

128 works under Water Security, 111 under Core Rural Infrastructure, 98 under Livelihood-related Infrastructure and 38 under Disaster Preparedness
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 8:29AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Rural Development has notified the Schedule of Permissible Works under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) [VB–G RAM G] Act, 2025, providing for 375 permissible works under the new rural works framework.
The new Schedule represents a 41 percent expansion over the 266 works under the previous framework.
The works have been reorganised around four thematic pillars — Water Security, Core Rural Infrastructure, Livelihood-related Infrastructure and Special Works for Extreme Weather Events and Disaster Preparedness.
The new framework seeks to move beyond a conventional list of asset types and align wage employment with the creation of durable rural assets and measurable development outcomes. Every work will originate through a bottom-up, decentralized planning process under the Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan, approved by the Gram Sabha, and will be tracked through the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack.
Water Security gets highest share with 128 works
The Water Security pillar comprises 128 works, the highest among the four categories. It includes check dams, gully plugs, underground dykes, recharge shafts, injection wells, rejuvenation of rivers, rivulets and nallahs, reclamation of waterlogged land and renovation of field water-distribution channels.
The Schedule also provides for drip irrigation, sprinkler systems, rooftop rainwater harvesting and tankas, along with newer interventions such as ice-stupas and artificial glaciers for water conservation and irrigation.
111 works for Core Rural Infrastructure
The Core Rural Infrastructure pillar comprises 111 works aimed at strengthening essential civic and community infrastructure in rural areas.
These include solar street lighting, waste-to-wealth recycling plants, greywater treatment units, segregation sheds, rural libraries, veterinary and rural health centres, Common Service Centres, multipurpose youth centres, community facilities and additional classrooms and laboratories in government schools.
The framework also provides for repair and maintenance of Jal Jeevan Mission water-supply infrastructure, along with rural parks, footpaths and other village-level amenities.
98 works to strengthen rural livelihoods and value chains
The new framework gives significantly greater emphasis to Livelihood-related Infrastructure, with 98 permissible works.
The category includes agro-processing and value-addition infrastructure, cleaning, grading and packaging units, cold storage facilities, mini flour mills, market yards, dairy infrastructure, mushroom cultivation sheds, sericulture sheds, poly-houses and aquaculture structures.
It also provides infrastructure for Self-Help Groups and their federations, including SHG worksheds, SHE Marts and federation buildings, as well as training-cum-skill development centres. The share of livelihood-related works rises substantially, accounting for
26 per cent of the total permissible works under the new framework, compared with 1.1 per cent under the previous framework.
38 works dedicated to Disaster Preparedness and Climate Resilience
For the first time, a dedicated category for disaster preparedness and extreme weather events has been incorporated into the rural works framework, comprising 38 works.
These include flood relief shelters, retaining walls, embankment strengthening, flood protection works, post-disaster restoration of rural roads and community assets, and forest-fire management measures such as fire lines and fuel-buffer zones.
The category is aimed at strengthening rural communities and assets against floods, cyclones, storms, droughts, landslides, forest fires and other extreme weather events.
Focus on Farmers, Vulnerable Households, Women and Rural Youth
The Schedule places particular emphasis on agriculture, vulnerable households, women and rural youth.
A total of 181 works are agriculture and allied works, including 52 individual-beneficiary works, covering water, land, plantation, livestock and other productive assets that can directly support farmers.
107 works are tagged for Antyodaya/vulnerable households, including 68 individual-beneficiary works. These include housing, sanitation, energy, irrigation, plantations, livestock shelters and other household-level assets.
The framework also includes 36 works related to Nari Shakti and 36 works related to Yuva Shakti, covering infrastructure for women’s collectives, SHGs and federations, youth centres, skill development and enterprise-linked infrastructure.
Inclusive and Future-Ready Rural Infrastructure
The new Schedule provides explicit provisions for Divyangjan accessibility, including construction of stairs and ramps in government buildings. It also includes emergency evacuation and relief shelters in border areas, renewable-energy infrastructure and circular-economy interventions such as waste-to-wealth recycling and greywater treatment.
Works to be planned through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans
Under VB–G RAM G, works will be planned through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans, based on local needs and approved by the Gram Sabha. The digital tracking mechanism through the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack will facilitate convergence of investments across Central, State and local schemes while helping avoid duplication.
The new Schedule thus seeks to align employment generation with water security, durable rural infrastructure, livelihood creation, climate resilience and inclusive development, contributing to the vision of a Viksit Bharat @2047.

title: India, Switzerland Strengthen Strategic Science & Technology Partnership; Dr. Jitendra Singh Holds Bilateral Meeting with Swiss President Guy Parmelin
subtitle:
Dr. Jitendra Singh and Swiss President Guy Parmelin discuss expanding long-term cooperation in science, research and innovation

India’s mission-mode approach in AI, quantum, biotechnology, space and deep ocean research opens new avenues for bilateral collaboration, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Indo-Swiss Research Framework, Joint Scientific Board and new institutional agreements to further strengthen research ecosystem

Switzerland earmarks CHF 45 million for further strengthening the Indo-Swiss research partnership
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today held a bilateral meeting with President of the Swiss Confederation, H.E. Guy Parmelin, in New Delhi, with discussions focused on further strengthening the longstanding India-Switzerland partnership in science, technology, research and innovation. The meeting focused on taking the bilateral S&T partnership into a more structured and long-term phase, with greater institutional engagement and cooperation in emerging areas of mutual interest.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India is increasingly adopting an interdisciplinary and mission-mode approach to Science and Technology, with national programmes bringing together expertise from different disciplines and ministries. He said Artificial Intelligence is being viewed as an enabling tool rather than a separate discipline, with the potential to contribute across diverse areas of science and technology.
Referring to India’s expanding S&T priorities, he spoke about the country’s work in biotechnology, vaccine development, genome sequencing, quantum technology, space and deep ocean research, as well as the emerging opportunities in the blue economy and bio-economy.
Dr. Jitendra Singh welcomed the progress towards the Indo-Swiss Research Framework (ISRF) and the Indo-Swiss Joint Scientific Board, which provide a stronger basis for taking bilateral S&T cooperation towards a strategic and long-term framework. He also welcomed the Letter of Intent between the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) and the Department of Science & Technology (DST) and the Implementation Agreement between the Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW) and DST, and said these initiatives would further strengthen institutional engagement and research collaboration between the two countries.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the cordial relationship between India and Switzerland makes it easier for the two countries to collaborate at different levels and stressed the need for a regular working arrangement to ensure sustained engagement and effective follow-up on areas of mutual interest. He said the two sides could continue working together to deepen cooperation in research, innovation and emerging technologies.
President Guy Parmelin said Switzerland sees India as a rapidly emerging global research and development power and seeks to position itself as a preferred long-term partner in education, research and innovation. Recalling the bilateral Science and Technology Agreement signed in 2003, he said the partnership has grown steadily and that Switzerland is committed to developing a more structured and long-term framework for cooperation.
President Parmelin said Switzerland has earmarked a further CHF 45 million for the partnership, and expressed the expectation of a corresponding commitment from India to further strengthen and consolidate the joint Indo-Swiss research framework. He expressed confidence that the two countries can achieve much more by building on their longstanding scientific partnership and working closely together.
The two sides also discussed Artificial Intelligence and its wider applications, with President Parmelin stressing the importance of ensuring that AI benefits countries across the Global South. He also invited Indian participation in the forthcoming Geneva AI Summit, reflecting the shared interest in expanding cooperation in emerging technologies and areas of global significance.
India and Switzerland have built more than two decades of cooperation in Science and Technology since the signing of the Inter-Governmental Agreement in 2003. The partnership has evolved through the Indo-Swiss Joint Research Programme and has expanded into areas including quantum technology, Artificial Intelligence, clean technology, renewable energy, ocean research and blue economy, advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, biomedical research, pandemic preparedness and space technologies.
The Indo-Swiss Research Framework now seeks to take this cooperation from a project-based model towards a more strategic, system-level partnership, with enhanced mobility, knowledge exchange and long-term cooperation.
The meeting was attended from the Swiss side by Dr. Martina Hirayama, State Secretary for Education, Research & Innovation (SERI); H.E. Maya Tissafi, Ambassador of Switzerland to India and Bhutan; Catherine von Wyl, Scientific Advisor, SERI; Prof. Dr. Torsten Schwede, President, Swiss National Science Foundation; Thomas Gfeller, Chief Executive Officer, Foundation Switzerland Innovation; Prof. Dr. Regula Jöhl, President, Zurich University of Applied Sciences; Joël François Mesot, President, ETH Zurich; and Leena Arora Kukreja, Science & Technology Counsellor, Embassy of Switzerland.
From the Indian side, Dr. Jitendra Singh was accompanied by Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology; Dr. Rajesh Sudhir Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology; Dr. Praveenkumar Somasundaram, Head, ICD, DST; and Dr. Ramkrishna Sahoo, Nodal, Swiss Desk, DST, during the meeting.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India and Switzerland, building on their cordial and longstanding relationship, can establish a regular working arrangement to sustain engagement and ensure continued follow-up on bilateral Science and Technology initiatives. He expressed confidence that the two countries can further deepen their partnership by working together across emerging areas of science, technology and innovation.

title: Indo-Swiss Research Framework to Give Fresh Impetus to Two Decades of Scientific Cooperation and Open New Avenues for Joint Research and Innovation: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Flagship Event celebrates two decades of India-Switzerland partnership and charts roadmap for deeper, structured and long-term collaboration

New framework to strengthen research networks, mobility, knowledge exchange and academia-industry linkages, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Explore and Academia-Industry Training programmes to create new opportunities for researchers, innovators and startups

DST-SNSF Letter of Intent and DST-ZHAW Implementation Arrangement mark new phase of bilateral S&T partnership
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today said that the Indo-Swiss Research Framework (ISRF) will give fresh impetus to the longstanding India-Switzerland Science, Technology and Innovation partnership and provide a structured platform for taking bilateral cooperation into new and emerging areas.
Addressing the inaugural Indo-Swiss Research Flagship Event 2026 in New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the event was an occasion not only to celebrate two decades of healthy and progressively expanding cooperation, but also to chart the way forward by diversifying the partnership into emerging areas of Science, Technology and Innovation and creating greater opportunities for researchers and innovators in both countries.
The Flagship Event, held at New Delhi, brought together H.E. Guy Parmelin, President of the Swiss Confederation; H.E. Maya Tissafi, Ambassador of Switzerland to India and Bhutan; Dr. Martina Hirayama, State Secretary for Education, Research & Innovation; Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology, and senior representatives of research institutions, funding agencies, universities and the wider innovation ecosystem.
The programme was structured around two broad themes, “Looking back on 20 Years of Impact and Excellence” and “Looking forward: Transforming Tomorrow Together”, reflecting both the achievements of the partnership and its future direction.
Dr. Jitendra Singh recalled that the formal foundation of India-Switzerland cooperation in Science and Technology was laid with the signing of the Inter-Governmental Agreement in 2003, followed by mechanisms for periodic review and expansion of the partnership. The Indo-Swiss Joint Research Programme, initiated in 2005, has since provided a platform for bringing together faculty and young researchers from both countries in areas of strategic relevance.
The Indo-Swiss Joint Committee on Science & Technology has also played an important role in reviewing ongoing cooperation and shaping future engagements, with seven rounds held so far, the latest in Bern in September 2025.
The Minister said the partnership has steadily expanded through the participation of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), in collaboration with Swiss institutions, particularly the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). This broad-based cooperation today spans research areas including mountain and glacier studies, geoscientific hazards, systems medicine, One Health and social sciences.
The expanding breadth of the partnership was also reflected in the event presentation, which showcased successive Indo-Swiss research initiatives across biomedical research, renewable energy, life sciences, systems medicine, social sciences and mountain research, with the 2026 initiatives further advancing cooperation in mountain hazards, social sciences and One Health. This progression reflects the growing thematic and institutional depth of India-Switzerland research cooperation.
Dr. Jitendra Singh spoke about strong collaboration between MoES and SNSF in mountain and glacier research and geoscientific hazards in mountain regions. The cooperation has already supported four Indo-Swiss projects covering glacier evolution, ice nucleating particles, water vapour isotopes and debris-glacier interactions, with the partnership subsequently expanded towards geoscientific hazards.
He also referred to the growing engagement in One Health between SNSF, DBT and ICMR, as well as cooperation between ICSSR and SNSF in areas such as digital governance, AI ethics and the social impact of Artificial Intelligence, inequality, justice and inclusion, mobility and social integration, and economic transformation.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Indo-Swiss Research Framework represents a new and more strategic phase in the relationship, moving the partnership towards a structured, system-level approach to long-term cooperation. The framework is designed to strengthen mobility, knowledge exchange, research networking and sustained collaboration, while opening new avenues for cooperation aligned with national priorities and globally relevant areas of Science, Technology and Innovation.
As part of this forward-looking agenda, the Minister welcomed new initiatives including “Explore”, aimed at building new research networks with the vision of developing larger consortia, and the Academia-Industry Training (AIT) programme for science-based innovators. The event presentation also showcased the forthcoming Explore programme, scheduled to open in November 2026 as a co-funded SNSF-DST initiative, with a 9–12-month duration and support for travel, networking and small equipment to help new ideas in basic science develop into larger research opportunities.
The Minister also welcomed the Letter of Intent between DST and SNSF and the Implementation Arrangement between DST and Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW). The LoI will support exploratory scientific collaboration, future joint research and long-term cooperation across mutually agreed priority areas, while the Implementation Arrangement will advance cooperation in innovation, technology transfer and entrepreneurship through the Indo-Swiss Academia-Industry Training (AIT India) programme.

title: A decade of cosmic flickering reveals new clues about a rare giant binary black hole system
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 2:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A new study has tracked the changing brightness and colour of the peculiar blazar OJ 287 over 10 years, offering fresh insights into its powerful emission and the behaviour of its central black holes.
OJ 287 is a rare astronomical object about 4 billion light years away from the Earth,
that contains two supermassive black holes (SMBHs) at its center, orbiting around each other in a twelve-year orbit, forming a binary system. SMBHs can have masses ranging from millions to billions of times that of the Sun. OJ 287 is a blazar, which produces powerful jets of plasma moving at nearly the speed of light and directed toward Earth. Blazars show strong and rapidly changing emission across the electromagnetic spectrum, from radio waves to gamma-rays.
The blazar produces a distinctive double-peaked pattern in its brightness over time. This periodic behaviour was discovered in 1988 by a team of scientists from Finland using nearly 100 years of optical observations dating back to 1880. Since then, astronomers around the world have continued to observe OJ 287 to track its 12-year cycle of double-peaked outbursts to get a complete picture of its orbital motion.
A multi-institutional study was carried out, co-ordinated by scientists from Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES), Nainital, an autonomous institution of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), to capture the most recent 12-year optical outbursts (periodic/quasi-periodic pattern) between 2015 and 2019.
The study led by Dr. Alok C. Gupta, from ARIES included a team of 106 scientists from 18 countries (India, Bulgaria, Chile, China, Crimea, Finland, Georgia, Germany, Italy, Japan, Russia, Serbia, Spain, Sweden, Tajikistan, the UK, the USA, and the West Indies) and 48 research institutions/universities carried out optical observation of the source using two dozen telescopes from 2015 to 2025.
Fig 1
:
Artistic illustration of the binary black hole system in OJ 287.
Credit: Lankeshwar Dey et al. 2018
The decade-long optical observation campaign supported by observations in other parts of the electromagnetic (EM) spectrum using several ground- and space-based telescopes produced the most extensive and densely sampled optical time-series data of OJ 287 obtained over the past 150 years.
The data tracked how OJ 287 has evolved across different timescales—from long-term changes spanning years to rapid variations occurring over much shorter periods. The study provides one of the most extensive multiband optical datasets available for this peculiar object.
The data obtained from the in the complete EM spectrum helped solve key problems like determine
the positions of the two black holes relative to each other at different times, understand how the brightness, spectrum, and polarization of OJ 287 changed over different timescales, search for evidence of emission from the smaller black hole and explore the nature and behaviour of this unique binary black hole system.
The study was preceded by a series of research papers led by Dr. A. C. Gupta and Prof. Mauri J. Valtonen, University of Turku, Finland Since 2017.
Fig 2
:
The black holes in orbit around each other. Both black holes have jets associated with them: the larger one with reddish colour, and the smaller one with a yellowish colour jet.
Credit: NASA/JPL–Caltech/R. Hurt (IPAC) and M. Mugrauer (AIU Jena)
Using eight optical spectra in the low-flux states of OJ 287 taken from 2017 October 21 to 2017 November 22, from Steward Observatory, USA the central black hole mass was estimated to be at least 3.89 billion solar mass from the [O III] emission line width. The study also provided insights into the emission mechanism of this binary black hole system and its importance for multimessenger astronomy (coordinated simultaneous observations in different electromagnetic bands from various ground and space based observing facilities) which entails combining different signals—like light, gravitational waves, neutrinos, and cosmic rays from the same source. These findings have expanded the scientific scope of OJ 287 beyond the study of its binary nature.
By bringing together a decade of optical observations, the study strengthens the picture of OJ 287 as a dynamic and extreme cosmic laboratory. Continued monitoring of the object across different wavelengths could help scientists better understand the physics of relativistic jets, the behaviour of supermassive binary black holes, and the possible connections between electromagnetic and gravitational-wave signals.

title: From Waste Picking to Self-Reliance:
subtitle: Mekala Yesamma’s Journey towards Economic Empowerment
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 7:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Financial assistance can play an important role in helping individuals from disadvantaged communities establish sustainable livelihoods and improve their economic condition. Timely support for self-employment can create new income opportunities, strengthen family financial security and promote greater dignity in livelihood.
Ms. Mekala Yesamma, aged 33, belongs to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community and had been working as a waste picker in the Guntur Municipal Corporation for nearly 12 years. Coming from a financially disadvantaged family, she could not attend school and remained illiterate. Her family faced persistent economic hardships, while limited income and restricted access to opportunities made it difficult for her to meet household needs and secure a better future for her children.
On 19 June 2023, Ms. Yesamma, along with one other member, received financial assistance under the
Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY)
of the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation through Navajeevan Organisation. The assistance was provided in the form of capital subsidy for a group project to procure an
Open Nallah Cleaner (Tractor-Mounted)
. The total project cost was Rs. 16,99,952, supported by a loan of Rs. 10,24,964 and capital subsidy of Rs. 6,74,988.
Before receiving the assistance, Ms. Yesamma earned approximately Rs. 8,000 per month through waste-picking activities. With the support provided under the SUY scheme and the resulting livelihood opportunity, she now earns an additional Rs. 10,000 per month, taking her total monthly income to approximately Rs. 18,000. The increase in income has strengthened her ability to meet household expenses, support her children's education and improve the overall standard of living of her family.
The support provided under the SUY scheme has significantly improved Ms. Yesamma’s socio-economic condition and provided her with an opportunity to pursue a more productive and dignified livelihood. The intervention has enhanced her financial security and confidence while reducing her dependence on limited sources of income.
Expressing her gratitude,
Ms. Mekala Yesamma said,
"The financial assistance under the SUY scheme has helped me improve my livelihood and increase my monthly income. It has made it easier for me to meet my family’s needs, support my children’s education and work towards a more secure future."
Ms. Mekala Yesamma’s journey demonstrates how timely financial assistance and livelihood support can enable individuals from disadvantaged communities to improve their earning capacity and move towards economic self-reliance. Her experience reflects the role of SUY in creating sustainable livelihood opportunities and promoting dignity, financial security and a stronger, more self-reliant society.

title: From Addiction To Independence
subtitle: Thoubal, Manipur’s L. Delay Rebuilds His Life Through ODIC Support
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Timely counselling, medical assistance, rehabilitation and family support can play an important role in helping individuals overcome substance dependence, rebuild their confidence and return to productive livelihoods. Targeted intervention can also help beneficiaries restore family relationships, develop a disciplined lifestyle and move towards greater social and economic self-reliance.
At the age of 24,
L. Delay (name changed)
, an OBC beneficiary from Thoubal, Manipur, was struggling with alcohol dependence that had gradually affected his education, family relationships and emotional well-being. He began consuming alcohol after completing Class 12, initially under peer pressure. Over time, occasional consumption developed into a serious dependence, with alcohol becoming a daily necessity. His addiction had a significant impact on his education and family life. Frequent quarrels at home and the stigma associated with his condition further deepened his distress.
Following a family conflict, L. Delay left home and began staying with his close relative in Bishnupur district. Recognising his need for professional assistance, he was brought by his relative to the nearby
Outreach and Drop In Centre (ODIC), Nambol Phoijing Makha, Bishnupur District, Manipur
,
where he received timely support and rehabilitation.
The ODIC provided L. Delay with a comprehensive package of support, including home detoxification, medical assistance, psychological counselling, behavioural rehabilitation and family counselling. He was also provided guidance to strengthen his ability to resist peer pressure, along with vocational support and assistance in rebuilding his social and family relationships. The structured intervention enabled him to address the underlying challenges associated with his alcohol dependence while gradually restoring his confidence and sense of purpose.
Over a period of three months of structured intervention and continued support, L. Delay successfully recovered from alcohol dependence. The counselling and rehabilitation process helped him develop a more disciplined lifestyle and make a firm commitment to remain free from alcohol. Continued family support also played an important role in helping him regain stability and reconnect with his responsibilities.
Today, L. Delay is working as a salesman at a large store in Kakching Bazar, earning a stable salary and contributing to his household. From a period marked by financial instability, family conflict and alcohol dependence, he has moved towards productive employment, financial independence and a more stable life.
L. Delay’s journey demonstrates how timely intervention, counselling, medical care, family support and vocational rehabilitation can help individuals overcome substance dependence and return to mainstream social and economic life. His experience reflects the importance of accessible rehabilitation services in enabling individuals to rebuild their lives with discipline, dignity and renewed purpose.

title: An Approach Paper on Expanding the scope and coverage for the Index of Services Production
subtitle: MoSPI invites comments/ feedback from stakeholders on the Approach Paper
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The services sector has firmly established itself as the primary engine of India's economic growth, driving more than half of the national Gross Value Added (GVA). To monitor this vital performance accurately, MoSPI initiated a monthly compilation of the ISP for the formal sector with 2024–25 as the base year, on a trial basis in July 2026.
The initial framework tracks 19 broad service sub-sectors—relying on high-frequency administrative data sources and data of outward supplies from GST which collectively accounted for approximately 60 per cent of services-sector GVA. However, core government tasks, non-market activities and GST-exempt services are excluded from the present framework.
To bridge these gaps and build a truly comprehensive Index of Services Sector, the Ministry intends to expand the scope of ISP, further. With this aim, MoSPI has published an
‘Approach paper on Expanding the scope and coverage for the Index of Services Production’
.
The approach paper details methodologies to onboard three major service areas that were previously left out: Education, Human Health & Residential Care, and Public Administration & Defence. Together, these three vital sectors represent nearly 21 per cent of services GVA for the 2024–25 period. By successfully incorporating them, MoSPI will elevate the total coverage of the monthly ISP to approximately 78.4 per cent of the entire services-sector GVA.
This expanded framework will enable aggregation of the sub-sectoral indices into a unified, all-encompassing Index of Services Production that provides a representative reflection of short-term movements of India's services sector.
MoSPI invites views and comments from experts, academicians, central government ministries/departments, state governments, financial institutions and other stakeholders on the proposed methodology. The Approach Paper is available on the MoSPI’s website www.mospi.gov.in. Comments and suggestions may be sent to the email to ddgec.esd@mospi.gov.in by 16th October, 2026.

content:
The first meeting of the Development Council for Textile Industry (DCTI) was held on 6th October, 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, under the chairpersonship of Secretary, Ministry of Textiles, Smt. Neelam Shami Rao. The Council, constituted as the apex consultative platform of Government, industry and stakeholders, convened to deliberate upon its mandate of advising the Government on the orderly growth and development of the textile industry.
The meeting was attended by Senior Officers of the Ministry, representatives of Industry Associations, Export Promotion Councils, Research Associations, State Governments and Sector Experts.
Addressing the Council, the Chair underscored that the textiles and apparel sector continues to be among the largest employment generators and export earners for the country and called for a coordinated, whole-of-value-chain approach towards production, innovation and global market access. The deliberations at the meeting focused on the following key areas:
Production and Productivity: Capacity addition, modernisation, scale and cost competitiveness across the fibre, yarn, fabric, processing and apparel segments, with emphasis on addressing gaps across the value chain.
Research and Development: Strengthening industry–research linkages, fostering innovation in new-age fibres and technical textiles, and facilitating faster commercialisation of R&D through Research Associations and institutions.
Exports and Market Access: Diversification of products and markets, leveraging trade agreements, and addressing quality, compliance and logistics-related constraints faced by exporters.
Raw Material and Input Availability: Ensuring stable and competitive availability of cotton, man-made fibres, yarn, dyes and chemicals, supported by effective market intelligence.
Investment, Skilling and Sustainability: Promoting ease of doing business, strengthening support for MSMEs, workforce skilling, and adoption of sustainable and circular practices.
Members shared sector-specific suggestions on each of the above themes and welcomed the institutionalised industry - Government interface provided by the Council.
The Council agreed to constitute Working Groups/Sub Committees on priority themes and to meet at regular intervals to review progress. The Council’s recommendations will inform the Ministry’s policy and programme interventions and are aimed at:
higher domestic production, improved productivity and a more integrated, scale-oriented value chain;
faster translation of research into industry practice, including in the areas of technical textiles and new-age fibres;
sustained growth in textile and apparel exports through wider market and product diversification; and
greater investment, employment generation and a stronger and more sustainable domestic ecosystem.
The Chair thanked the members for their valuable inputs and reiterated the Government’s commitment towards a collaborative and industry-facing approach for the sustained growth of the sector.

He also stressed the importance of understanding the challenges faced by the communities from the field level officials, which will enable the central government to come up with solutions and practical guidelines.
The Hon’ble Minister of States for Tribal affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey addressed the gathering through video conferencing. He emphasized the need for simple, transparent, time-bound and citizen-friendly processes while maintaining effective safeguards against fraudulent claims.
Smt Ranjana Chopra, Secretary Tribal Affairs expressed hope that the two-day conclave will bring out common challenges, replicable best practices, role of digitization of records, streamlined documentation, online tracking, effective grievance redressal and stronger inter-State verification mechanisms.
More than 75 delegates from around 30 states/UTs are attending the conclave. The Conclave will have technical sessions, open discussions and experience sharing sessions.
The deliberations of the Conclave are expected to contribute towards strengthening the implementation of constitutional safeguards and promoting effective, transparent and accessible protection and services for tribal communities.

The Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) 2027, a flagship youth engagement initiative of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), has successfully completed the Viksit Bharat Quiz. The Quiz drew an overwhelming response from young Indians across the country, with 1,45,26,013 attempts recorded during the selection process.
The VBYLD 2027 aims to provide young citizens with a structured, merit-based platform to share their ideas, perspectives and innovative solutions towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The initiative aligns with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to create opportunities for talented youth to participate in public life and contribute to nation-building.
A Merit-Based National Youth Leadership Journey
VBYLD 2027 follows a structured, multi-stage selection process designed to identify and nurture youth leadership from the grassroots to the national level. The Viksit Bharat Challenge follows the pathway:
Viksit Bharat Quiz → Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge → District PPT Championship → State/UT VBYLD → National VBYLD
The Viksit Bharat Quiz, the first stage of the VBYLD 2027 selection process, was conducted on the MY Bharat portal from 17 August to 30 September 2026, with a corresponding Quiz also hosted on the MyGov platform. The Quiz comprised 20 questions, with a maximum score of 20 marks and a time limit of 10 minutes.
About 5.7 lakh youth who qualified in the Quiz round will proceed to the next stage, the Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge, and submit a 500-word essay on the MY Bharat portal on the theme designated for the region. The themes for the essay and presentation rounds are as under. The detailed mapping of States with themes is available on MY Bharat Portal:
Future Governance, Urban Transformation & Citizen Services
Climate Security, Borders & Sustainable Mountain Development
Demographic Dividend & Human Capital Development
Sustainable Industrialization & Resource-led Growth
Act East, Connectivity & Cultural Leadership
Manufacturing, Entrepreneurship & Green Growth
Tribal Leadership, Natural Resources & Inclusive Development
Innovation Economy, Tourism & Creative Industries
Technology, Innovation, Future Readiness
Blue Economy, Human Capital & Global Competitiveness
Essays may be written in any of 23 languages on the MY Bharat portal till 15th October, 2026. The most promising young contributors will be shortlisted for an in-person presentation round at the district level, which will be conducted across all districts for the first time. Selected participants will then proceed to the State/UT VBYLD to present at that stage.  Participants selected from all States/UTs under 10 regional themes will form part of the National contingent of the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD).

title: “Yuva Shakti is the Strength of Viksit Bharat”: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
subtitle: MY Bharat’s Points, Rewards and Recognition Mechanism to Turn Youth Participation into Recognition, Opportunity and Leadership
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 OCT 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), is operationalising a Points, Rewards and Recognition (PRR) Mechanism on the MY Bharat Portal to recognise and encourage sustained participation of young people in volunteering, experiential learning, youth development initiatives and other nation-building activities.
Highlighting the importance of youth participation in the nation-building process, Union Minister for Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya said, “Yuva Shakti is the strength of Viksit Bharat. Through MY Bharat’s PRR mechanism, the Modi Government is turning youth participation into recognition, opportunity and leadership.”
The PRR mechanism introduces a structured, milestone-based system through which youth will receive recognition, rewards and opportunities based on the points accumulated through their engagement on the MY Bharat Portal. The initiative seeks to motivate young people to sustain their participation in volunteering, experiential learning, civic engagement and youth development activities, while encouraging them to strive towards higher milestones.
Under the mechanism, youth achieving 1,000 points will receive a formal MY Bharat Letter of Recognition, signed by the Director, MY Bharat Division. At the 2,500-point milestone, eligible participants will be recognised through the official MY Bharat social media handles, subject to a consent-based mechanism for publication of their name, photograph and MY Bharat ID.
Youth attaining 5,000 points will be featured in a dedicated MY Bharat Digital Hall of Fame on the MY Bharat Portal. The Hall of Fame will showcase the achiever’s name, MY Bharat ID, photograph and a brief profile drawn from the public profile. A facility for other users to send messages to achievers may also be explored, subject to appropriate safeguards.
The mechanism provides progressively enhanced rewards at higher milestones. Youth achieving 7,500 points will receive the hardbound book Modi@20. Those reaching 10,000 points will be eligible to receive a signed hardbound copy of The Golden Road: How Ancient India Transformed the World by William Dalrymple, signed by the Hon’ble Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports. At the 20,000-point milestone, eligible achievers will receive a signed hardbound copy of Treasures of India: From Antiquity to Modernity by DK, signed by the Hon’ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports.
The higher milestones under the PRR mechanism are designed to provide young achievers with opportunities for direct interaction with senior leadership. At the 50,000-point milestone, eligible youth will have an opportunity to meet the Hon’ble Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports during an upcoming edition of the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) or another suitable major youth engagement event. The eligible achievers will be identified from the Portal and their details verified by MY Bharat Headquarters.
At the highest proposed milestone of 1,00,000 points, eligible youth will have an opportunity to meet the Hon’ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports during an upcoming edition of VBYLD. The selected youth will be identified through the MY Bharat Portal and their details verified by MY Bharat Headquarters. The felicitation of youth achieving the 50,000 and 1,00,000-point milestones is proposed to commence from October 2027.
The PRR mechanism establishes a progressive pathway that begins with formal recognition and digital visibility and extends to tangible rewards and opportunities to engage with national youth leadership platforms. Through the initiative, MY Bharat seeks to create a sustained culture of participation, service and leadership among India’s youth.
The initiative reinforces the vision of “Samarth Yuva, Viksit Bharat”, recognising that active and empowered youth are central to India’s journey towards a developed nation. By acknowledging individual contributions and creating opportunities for further engagement, the PRR mechanism seeks to inspire young citizens to continue their journey of leadership, community service and nation-building through MY Bharat.

title: Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA)
subtitle: A comprehensive National Transport Master Plan
date:

content:
India's Expanding Transport and Logistics Network
As India’s economy grows, so does the need to move goods efficiently across the country. Meeting this requirement calls for transport networks that are well connected and planned as an integrated system. To support these growing requirements, the Government on
6 October 2026
approved the setting up of the
Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA)
. ITLA will serve as a specialised institutional mechanism for
research, planning, project appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment across transportation and logistics
.
With the expansion of the transport and logistics networks, ITLA will
support long-term integrated planning and post-implementation impact assessment of infrastructure projects
. It will complement existing initiatives such as the
PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
and the
National Logistics Policy
.
Roles and Responsibilities
ITLA will undertake a range of responsibilities covering integrated planning, project appraisal, monitoring, data analytics, logistics policy, capacity building and research. Its key responsibilities include:
National Apex Institution:
ITLA will
serve as the apex institution for integrated transport and logistics planning, research, project appraisal and monitoring. It will provide
policy support and data analytics
to strengthen coordinated decision-making across the transport sector.
Long-Term National Transport Master Plan
: The authority will prepare a comprehensive
National Transport Master Plan
with a planning horizon of
10 years or more
. It will cover
roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics
.
Integrated Planning Framework:
It will
evaluate short-term sectoral plans with a horizon of around five years and annual plans of transport Ministries. Also, it will ensure their alignment with the
National Transport Master Plan
and promote
multimodal infrastructure development
.
Technical Appraisal of Major Projects:
ITLA will undertake technical appraisal of Government of India infrastructure projects costing
₹500 crore or more
. Financial appraisal will continue to be carried out through the existing financial appraisal mechanisms.
Monitoring and Impact Assessment:
It will
monitor transport and infrastructure projects costing
above ₹500 crore
and provide a coordinated mechanism for issue resolution. It will also undertake
post-implementation impact assessments
to evaluate project outcomes and performance.
National Transport Data Repository (NTDR):
The authoirty will develop a unified transport data repository by integrating relevant transport and logistics datasets from multiple sources. These include
GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS-based systems and urban traffic management systems
. The data will support freight-flow and origin-destination analysis for planning, monitoring and impact assessment.
Logistics Policy Support:
It will advise and assist in the review and updating of the National Logistics Policy (2022).
Capacity Building:
It will contribute to capacity building, training, and skilling in the logistics sector.
Research and Innovation:
It will promote research & innovations in transport and logistics sectors.
Key Benefits
ITLA will strengthen integrated planning, coordination, data use and institutional capacity across the transport and logistics ecosystem:
Central institutional mechanism:
ITLA will serve as a central institutional mechanism for research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment in transport and logistics. This approach follows
global practice
in line with other countries such as Korea, Japan, the US, China and Australia.
Unified infrastructure planning:
ITLA will act as the apex coordinating agency for unified infrastructure planning. It will also prepare a comprehensive
National Transport Master Plan.
Inter-ministerial coordination:
ITLA will enable synergy and coordination among ministries dealing with transport and logistics. This will cover infrastructure planning, appraisal, monitoring and evaluation.
Integrated data repository:
ITLA will create a unified transport data repository. This will support evidence-based planning, research and innovation.
Institutional capacity building:
ITLA will strengthen capacity in research, planning, big data integration, project monitoring and evaluation. It will also promote the adoption of international best practices.
Supporting India’s Vision 2047
As India’s transport and logistics networks continue to expand,
seamless multimodal connectivity and efficient infrastructure
will become increasingly important. ITLA will strengthen integrated planning, project appraisal, monitoring and data-driven decision-making across the transport and logistics ecosystem. By improving infrastructure efficiency, supporting multimodal connectivity and building institutional capacity,
ITLA will contribute to India’s Vision 2047 and a more competitive logistics ecosystem
.

content:
A New Growth Capital Push for SMEs
Classification of SMEs
Enterprises are classified as micro, small or medium based on investment in plant and machinery or equipment, and annual turnover. Under the latest criteria (effective from April 2025), a
small enterprise
has investment of up to
₹25 crore
and turnover of up to
₹100 crore
. A
medium enterprise
has investment of up to
₹125 crore
and turnover of up to
₹500 crore
.
Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)
form the backbone of the Indian economy, contributing to employment, exports, manufacturing output and innovation. To support their growth, the Union Cabinet has approved a commitment of
₹10,000 crore
towards establishing the
SME Growth Fund (SGF).
The Fund will provide patient equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability. It aims to support the emergence of champion enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains.
As
part of the holistic set of announcements made under the Union Budget 2026-27
, the initiative focuses on providing
equity, liquidity and professional support
to the MSME ecosystem.
India’s MSME Ecosystem
Contribution to the Economy:
According to the Economic Survey 2025-26,
MSMEs account for 31.1% of GDP, 35.4% of manufacturing output and 48.58% of exports
.
Expanding Formal MSME Base:
As of
6 October 2026
, total MSME registrations under
Udyam and the Udyam Assist Platform (UAP)
reached
~9.78 crore
. Registered MSMEs have also reported
~43.28
crore employment opportunities.
Women’s Participation in MSMEs:
Female-owned enterprises account for
37.6%
of total registrations.
MSMEs Across Key Economic Activities:
The registered base is spread across trading, services and manufacturing.
Trading
accounts for around
~4.08 crore registrations,
followed by
services
at
~3.77 crore
and
manufacturing
at
~1.93 crore
.
Operational Framework of the SME Growth Fund
What are AIFs?
An Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) is a
privately pooled fund
established in India that raises money from investors and invests it according to a
defined policy
.
Investment Structure and Selection
The SME Growth Fund is designed as a
direct equity investment fund
and will operate in the form of
Alternative Investment Fund (AIF)
established under the SGF framework.
Strategic Focus of the SME Growth Fund
Manufacturing at the Core:
A major share of the SME Growth Fund’s allocations will be directed towards
small and medium manufacturing-focused enterprises
.
The Fund is intended to support firms seeking to expand
manufacturing capacity,
adopt
advanced technologies,
improve
productivity
and strengthen
export competitiveness
.
Extending Growth to Industrial Clusters:
The Fund will also consider SMEs operating in industrial clusters in
Tier-II and Tier-III cities
.
This is expected to support balanced
regional industrial development,
strengthen
local supply chains
and generate
quality employment opportunities
.
Why SMEs Need a Dedicated Growth Fund?
Despite the wide presence of MSMEs across the economy, existing equity funds largely focus on early-stage enterprises covering Micro enterprises. This creates scope to further expand access to growth equity capital for Small and Medium Enterprises.
Such capital becomes important as SMEs seek to scale further.  It can also help enterprises navigate
critical inflection points in their growth journey
and move towards greater scale and competitiveness. These investments can support promising SMEs in developing into industry leaders.
How Long-Term Growth Capital Enables SME Expansion
Scale operations
Undertake acquisitions
Foster innovation
Integrate into global value chains
Adopt advanced technology
Undertake strategic investments
Invest in manufacturing capacity
Expand into international markets
Impact on Innovation, Growth and Employment
The Fund is expected to strengthen the growth of high-potential SMEs across key sectors. Its impact aims to extend to enterprise scale-up, competitiveness and employment generation.
It is expected to
support enterprises operating in sectors of national importance
.
It will also help SMEs
expand capacity
and
scale operations
, supporting
employment generation
.
The initiative aims to build a
strong pipeline of Indian companies
with the scale, manufacturing capability and competitiveness required to become
sectoral champions
.
A Broader Support Ecosystem for MSMEs
MSMEs receive support across several areas, including finance, employment generation, skills, technology, end-to-end assistance and public procurement.
Focus Area
Key Implementing Schemes
Credit and Finance Support
Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
Employment generation
Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
End-to-end support
PM Vishwakarma
Training and Entrepreneurship Development
MSME Skilling, Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programme (ESDP), ASPIRE
Technology Infrastructure and Enablement
Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP), Zero Defect (ZED) Scheme, Tool Room and Tech Centre
Public Procurement
MSME SAMBANDH, SC/ ST Hub
Conclusion
The SME Growth Fund complements ongoing efforts to strengthen the SME sector through
reforms, digitalisation, credit support and ease of doing business measures
. By catalysing investments, the Fund will
promote innovation-led industrialisation
while advancing the vision of
Atmanirbhar Bharat
and
Viksit Bharat@2047
.
This support for smaller enterprises reflects
India’s broader effort to make growth more inclusive
, with opportunities extending across the country.

content:
Asian Games 2026 at a Glance
The Asian Games, also known as
Asiad,
are the biggest sports competition in Asia,
held once every four years
. They are
organized by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)
and currently have
45 participating countries or regions.
The
20th Asian Games were held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4, 2026
. The official slogan was “
Imagine One Asia.
” This is the third time that Japan has hosted the Asian Games, following the earlier editions held in
Tokyo (1958)
and
Hiroshima (1994)
.
This major event was spread over
16 days
of intense world-class competitions. It featured
43 sports
and
71 disciplines
in a grand showcase of athletic excellence. A total of
1,407 medals were awarded across 469 exciting events
during the Games.
Alongside the Asian Games,
Japan also hosting the 5th Asian Para Games
from October 18 to October 24, 2026, in Aichi-Nagoya. This marks the first time Japan has hosted the Para Games.
Understanding the Asian Games 2026 Emblem
The colour and design of the official emblem combine local and cultural significance with dynamics of sports. While the curves represent liveliness, the purple, gold, and green centre lines evoke the image of people uniting and advancing towards a bright red sun-the official symbol of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). P
urple
represents Aichi’s prefectural flower, the iris;
gold
symbolizes Kinshachi, the iconic golden tiger-fish roof ornaments of Nagoya Castle; and
green
reflects the strong environmental consciousness of Aichi-Nagoya, fostered through landmark events such as EXPO 2005 Aichi, COP10, and the UNESCO World Conference on ESD. The emblem contains the first letters of Asia, Aichi and Nagoya initials: “A” is depicted in the purple curve and centre line, “N” in purple and gold.
Asian Games 2026 Official Mascot
“HONOHON,” the mascot of the 20th Asian Games, represents the fiery passion of athletes.  The name is derived from the Japanese word ‘
honoho’
, connected to the origin of the Japanese word for flame. It’s design is inspired by the
Shachihoko,
one of the distinctive symbols of the Nagoya Castle and guarding deity of Aichi-Nagoya.
First Asian Games in 1951: India’s Founding Role
India's connection with the Asian Games goes back to the very beginning, when the first edition was held in New Delhi in 1951. This was done against the backdrop of post-World War II efforts to strengthen ties among Asian nations, with several regions of Asia having been recently decolonized. The idea of an Asian sporting competition was mooted by India as a means to display unity and rebuild the bonds between Asian nations that the war had broken
.
The idea of the Asian Games was first conceived by Prof. G.D. Sondhi, a member of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for India. The suggestion for holding the Asian Games was first made at a conference of Asian Countries held in New Delhi in 1947, and it was decided to call it the Asian Games.
The inaugural Asian Games were held in New Delhi in March, 1951. President Rajendra Prasad declared them open at the National Stadium.
Eleven nations sent 489 athletes to compete across six sports
at that first edition
. India finished second in the medal table that year, behind Japan. Since then, the Games have become a big event that fosters friendship through sports and contributes to world peace by recognizing diversity.
India's Contingent at Aichi-Nagoya 2026
India fielded one of its largest-ever multi-sport delegations at the Asian Games 2026, with a
501-athlete contingent
across
36 sporting disciplines
.
More than 300 athletes in the contingent were making their Asian Games debut
.
A grand send-off ceremony was held in New Delhi on 8 September 2026, ahead of the team’s departure. Union Minister Dr Mandaviya, Indian Olympic Association (IOA) President Dr P.T. Usha and Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav attended the event, and the official contingent jersey was unveiled. The Indian Olympic Association organised the event.
Dr. Mandaviya (Centre), along with IOA President Dr. P.T. Usha (right) & Secretary (Sports) Hari Ranjan Rao (left), unveiled the official contingent jersey ahead of the Asian Games 2026.
Image Source: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
At the opening ceremony
on 19 September 2026,
double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and Kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat
led India's parade.
India's Gold Medal Triumph at Aichi-Nagoya 2026
India’s campaign at the 2026 Asian Games was highlighted by a 21-gold-medal haul, anchored by strong performances across precision events and team sports.
Archery
led the gold tally with
5 titles
, supported by
Shooting
and
Boxing,
which each won
3 gold medals
. In team sports, India executed a sweeping "gold rush" across
Cricket
,
Hockey
, and
Kabaddi
, securing
2 gold medals in each sport
. Standout performances included the
men's cricket team
defeating Pakistan by 19 runs in the final, the
men's hockey team
retaining their continental title with a resounding 5-1 victory over Malaysia, and double gold victories across both the men's and women's
kabaddi
competitions. Further gold medals in
Wrestling (2), Athletics (1) and Golf (1)
brought India’s total to 21, reflecting the country’s strong and diverse performance across the continental sporting arena.
