India's Participation in the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games
The Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games will be held in Japan from 18 to 24 October 2026. Around 3,000 athletes from 45 National Paralympic Committees across Asia are expected to compete at these Games. The Games will feature eighteen Para sports.
India will participate through the Paralympic Committee of India, its recognised National Paralympic Committee for the Games. This will mark India's fifth appearance at the Asian Para Games, following its record 111-medal haul including 29 Gold medals at Hangzhou 2022 Asian Para Games. Out of the 111 medals, female athletes contributed 40 medals (36% of the medal tally). Previously, India had won 14 medals in the 2010 edition, 33 in 2014 and 72 in 2018.
From Grassroots to Global Podiums: India's Policy Push for Sports
Khelo Bharat Niti
The Government launched
Khelo Bharat Niti,
India's national sports policy, on 1 July 2025. It seeks to build a strong, inclusive, and performance-driven sports system. It focuses on bridging the rural-urban gap in training and facilities. It stresses community participation and partnerships to reduce training costs. The policy sets its sights on excellence at the 2036 Olympics. It links sports with school education under the National Education Policy 2020. It also supports women, tribal communities, and persons with disabilities.
Record Financial Support
The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated a record
₹
4,479.88 crore
to the sports ministry. This is up from
₹
1,219 crore
in 2013-14.  The Cabinet has also approved a revamped Khelo India scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31. With support to National Sports Federations, the combined outlay is
₹
36,441 crore
. Khelo India alone received
₹
924.35 crore for 2026
–
27
. Earlier, the scheme had a ₹3,790.50 crore outlay for 2021–22 to 2025–26. The Budget also earmarked
₹
500 crore for sports goods manufacturing
.
Finding Talent Early
Khelo India
is the flagship programme for grassroots sport. By July 2026, it had set up
1,067
Khelo India Centres. It has approved
349
new sports infrastructure projects worth
₹
3,176 crore
. It supports
2,745
Khelo India Athletes with coaching, equipment, medical care, and a monthly allowance. More than
63,000
athletes have competed in the Khelo India Games since 2018.
The
Khelo India Rising Talent Identification (KIRTI
) initiative identifies and nurtures talent among children aged 9 to 18 years. Its
174
Talent Assessment Centres use data tools for fair, merit-based selection.
Backing Top Athletes
The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)
supports India's athletes. It supports athletes through foreign training, international competitions, coaching camps, and specialised equipment. Athletes receive a
monthly stipend of ₹
50,000
. Junior athletes in the Development Group receive ₹25,000 a month. As of April 2026, TOPS supports
55 Core Athletes
,
62 Para Core Athletes
and
140 Development Athletes; in addition, 67 core athletes are in hockey
. TOPS played an important role in India's medals at the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games.
Education, Fitness and Fair Play
The
National Sports University
in Imphal was established in 2018. It offers education in sports science, technology, management and coaching.
The Fit India Movement encourages people to make fitness part of daily life. Parliament passed the
National Sports Governance Bill
in August 2025. It provides for a National Sports Board to recognise sports bodies. A National Sports Tribunal will settle sports disputes.
Beyond Aichi-Nagoya: India's Long Olympic Road
Aichi-Nagoya 2026 sits within India's broader roadmap toward the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and beyond. More than three hundred of India's five-hundred-plus athletes are making their Asian Games debut this year. This scale of debutant participation reflects the growing depth and expanding bench strength of Indian sport today.
The government has also outlined a ten-year plan investing over ₹36,000 crore to strengthen sports infrastructure nationwide. This investment aims to firmly establish India on the global sporting stage well before 2036. The Sports Ministry has called for a coordinated 360-degree approach involving federations, states and other stakeholders.
India's 85-medal campaign at Aichi-Nagoya, including 21 gold medals, marks another significant chapter in the country's sporting journey. With strong performances across traditional strengths and emerging disciplines, the Games have added further momentum to India's preparations for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and its longer-term sporting ambitions.
